  }

  @keyframes msgFadeIn {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); }
    to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
  }

  .message.user { flex-direction: row-reverse; }

  .msg-avatar {
    width: 36px;
    height: 36px;
    border-radius: 4px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    font-size: 16px;
    flex-shrink: 0;
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.3);
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.05);
    box-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(255,0,51,0.15);
  }

  .msg-bubble {
    max-width: 75%;
    padding: 14px 18px;
    border-radius: 6px;
    font-size: 14px;
    line-height: 1.7;
    position: relative;
  }

  .message.bot .msg-bubble {
    background: rgba(15,0,10,0.9);
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.2);
    border-left: 3px solid var(--neon-red);
    color: var(--text-secondary);
    box-shadow: 0 0 15px rgba(255,0,51,0.05);
  }

  .message.user .msg-bubble {
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.08);
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.3);
    color: var(--text-primary);
    text-align: right;
  }

  .msg-bubble b, .msg-bubble strong {
    color: var(--neon-red);
    text-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(255,0,51,0.4);
  }

  .msg-bubble code {
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 12px;
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.08);
    padding: 2px 6px;
    border-radius: 3px;
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.2);
    color: var(--neon-orange-red);
  }

  .msg-bubble pre {
    background: rgba(0,0,0,0.6);
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.2);
    border-left: 3px solid var(--neon-crimson);
    padding: 12px;
    border-radius: 4px;
    overflow-x: auto;
    margin: 10px 0;
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 12px;
    color: var(--neon-orange-red);
    line-height: 1.6;
  }

  .msg-time {
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 10px;
    color: var(--text-muted);
    margin-top: 4px;
    text-align: right;
  }

  /* Finding Cards inside chat */
  .finding-card {
    background: rgba(0,0,0,0.5);
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.3);
    border-radius: 6px;
    padding: 14px;
    margin: 10px 0;
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
  }

  .finding-card::before {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    left: 0;
    right: 0;
    height: 2px;
    background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--neon-red), var(--neon-crimson), var(--neon-orange-red));
    box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--neon-red);
  }

  .finding-severity {
    display: inline-block;
    font-family: 'Orbitron', monospace;
    font-size: 10px;
    font-weight: 700;
    padding: 3px 10px;
    border-radius: 2px;
    letter-spacing: 2px;
    margin-bottom: 8px;
  }

  .severity-critical {
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.2);
    color: var(--neon-red);
    border: 1px solid var(--neon-red);
    box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(255,0,51,0.4);
    animation: severityPulse 1.5s ease-in-out infinite;
  }

  .severity-high {
    background: rgba(220,20,60,0.2);
    color: var(--neon-crimson);
    border: 1px solid var(--neon-crimson);
    box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(220,20,60,0.3);
  }

  .severity-medium {
    background: rgba(255,69,0,0.15);
    color: var(--neon-orange-red);
    border: 1px solid var(--neon-orange-red);
  }

  .severity-pass {
    background: rgba(0,255,100,0.1);
    color: #00ff64;
    border: 1px solid #00ff64;
  }

  @keyframes severityPulse {
    0%, 100% { box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(255,0,51,0.4); }
    50% { box-shadow: 0 0 16px rgba(255,0,51,0.8); }
  }

  .finding-title {
    font-family: 'Orbitron', monospace;
    font-size: 12px;
    color: var(--text-primary);
    margin-bottom: 6px;
    letter-spacing: 1px;
  }

  .finding-detail {
    font-size: 12px;
    color: var(--text-muted);
    line-height: 1.6;
  }

  .finding-action-row {
    display: flex;
    gap: 8px;
    margin-top: 12px;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
  }

  .action-btn {
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 11px;
    padding: 6px 14px;
    border-radius: 3px;
    cursor: pointer;
    letter-spacing: 1px;
    border: 1px solid;
    background: transparent;
    transition: all 0.2s ease;
  }

  .btn-approve {
    color: #00ff64;
    border-color: #00ff64;
  }
  .btn-approve:hover {
    background: rgba(0,255,100,0.1);
    box-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(0,255,100,0.3);
  }

  .btn-reject {
    color: var(--neon-red);
    border-color: var(--neon-red);
  }
  .btn-reject:hover {
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.1);
    box-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(255,0,51,0.3);
  }

  .btn-evidence {
    color: var(--neon-orange-red);
    border-color: var(--neon-orange-red);
  }
  .btn-evidence:hover {
    background: rgba(255,69,0,0.1);
    box-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(255,69,0,0.3);
  }

  /* Typing indicator */
  .typing-indicator {
    display: flex;
    gap: 4px;
    align-items: center;
    padding: 8px 12px;
  }

  .typing-dot {
    width: 6px;
    height: 6px;
    background: var(--neon-red);
    border-radius: 50%;
    animation: typingBounce 1.2s ease-in-out infinite;
    box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--neon-red);
  }

  .typing-dot:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.2s; }
  .typing-dot:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 0.4s; }

  @keyframes typingBounce {
    0%, 60%, 100% { transform: translateY(0); }
    30% { transform: translateY(-8px); }
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════
     INPUT AREA
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════ */
  .input-area {
    padding: 16px 20px;
    background: rgba(5,0,4,0.95);
    border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.15);
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: 12px;
  }

  .quick-buttons {
    display: flex;
    gap: 8px;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
  }

  .quick-btn {
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 11px;
    padding: 6px 14px;
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.05);
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.25);
    color: var(--text-muted);
    border-radius: 3px;
    cursor: pointer;
    letter-spacing: 1px;
    transition: all 0.2s ease;
  }

  .quick-btn:hover {
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.1);
    border-color: var(--neon-red);
    color: var(--neon-red);
    box-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(255,0,51,0.2);
  }

  .input-row {
    display: flex;
    gap: 12px;
    align-items: flex-end;
  }

  .input-field {
    flex: 1;
    background: rgba(10,0,8,0.9);
    border: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.25);
    border-radius: 6px;
    padding: 14px 18px;
    font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif;
    font-size: 14px;
    color: var(--text-primary);
    resize: none;
    min-height: 52px;
    max-height: 150px;
    transition: all 0.3s ease;
    outline: none;
  }

  .input-field::placeholder {
    color: rgba(170,102,119,0.5);
    font-style: italic;
  }

  .input-field:focus {
    border-color: var(--neon-red);
    box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(255,0,51,0.15), inset 0 0 10px rgba(255,0,51,0.03);
  }

  .send-btn {
    width: 52px;
    height: 52px;
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.1);
    border: 1px solid var(--neon-red);
    color: var(--neon-red);
    border-radius: 6px;
    cursor: pointer;
    font-size: 20px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    transition: all 0.2s ease;
    box-shadow: 0 0 15px rgba(255,0,51,0.2);
    flex-shrink: 0;
  }

  .send-btn:hover {
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.2);
    box-shadow: 0 0 25px rgba(255,0,51,0.4);
    transform: scale(1.05);
  }

  .send-btn:active { transform: scale(0.95); }

  .input-footer {
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 10px;
    color: rgba(170,102,119,0.5);
    text-align: center;
    letter-spacing: 1px;
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════
     METRICS PANEL
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════ */
  .metrics-panel {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr));
    gap: 12px;
    margin-bottom: 30px;
  }

  .metric-card {
    background: var(--card-bg);
    border: 1px solid var(--card-border);
    padding: 16px;
    border-radius: 6px;
    text-align: center;
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
    transition: all 0.3s;
  }

  .metric-card:hover {
    border-color: rgba(255,0,51,0.4);
    box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(255,0,51,0.1);
  }

  .metric-value {
    font-family: 'Orbitron', monospace;
    font-size: 28px;
    font-weight: 900;
    color: var(--neon-red);
    text-shadow: 0 0 10px rgba(255,0,51,0.5);
    display: block;
    line-height: 1;
    margin-bottom: 6px;
  }

  .metric-label {
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 10px;
    color: var(--text-muted);
    letter-spacing: 2px;
    text-transform: uppercase;
  }

  .metric-bar {
    position: absolute;
    bottom: 0;
    left: 0;
    height: 2px;
    background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--neon-red), var(--neon-crimson));
    box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--neon-red);
    animation: metricLoad 2s ease-out forwards;
  }

  @keyframes metricLoad {
    from { width: 0%; }
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════
     AUDIT TRAIL PANEL
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════ */
  .audit-panel {
    background: rgba(5,0,4,0.95);
    border: 1px solid var(--card-border);
    border-radius: 6px;
    margin-bottom: 30px;
    overflow: hidden;
  }

  .audit-header {
    padding: 12px 16px;
    background: rgba(255,0,51,0.05);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--card-border);
    font-family: 'Orbitron', monospace;
    font-size: 11px;
    color: var(--neon-red);
    letter-spacing: 3px;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
  }

  .audit-log {
    padding: 12px 16px;
    max-height: 160px;
    overflow-y: auto;
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 11px;
    color: var(--text-muted);
    line-height: 2;
    scrollbar-width: thin;
    scrollbar-color: var(--neon-red-dim) transparent;
  }

  .audit-entry {
    display: flex;
    gap: 12px;
    animation: auditFade 0.3s ease;
  }

  @keyframes auditFade {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(-10px); }
    to { opacity: 1; transform: translateX(0); }
  }

  .audit-time { color: rgba(255,0,51,0.5); flex-shrink: 0; }

  .audit-action { color: var(--neon-red); flex-shrink: 0; }

  .audit-detail { color: var(--text-muted); }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════
     FOOTER
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════ */
  .footer {
    text-align: center;
    padding: 20px 0;
    font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace;
    font-size: 11px;
    color: rgba(170,102,119,0.4);
    letter-spacing: 2px;
    border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.08);
  }

  .footer span {
    color: rgba(255,0,51,0.4);
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════
     GLITCH EFFECT
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════ */
  .glitch {
    position: relative;
  }

  .glitch::before, .glitch::after {
    content: attr(data-text);
    position: absolute;
    top: 0; left: 0;
    width: 100%;
    height: 100%;
    font-family: inherit;
    font-size: inherit;
    font-weight: inherit;
    letter-spacing: inherit;
  }

  .glitch::before {
    color: rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.8);
    animation: glitch1 3s infinite;
    clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 33%, 0 33%);
    z-index: -1;
  }

  .glitch::after {
    color: rgba(220, 20, 60, 0.8);
    animation: glitch2 3s infinite;
    clip-path: polygon(0 67%, 100% 67%, 100% 100%, 0 100%);
    z-index: -1;
  }

  @keyframes glitch1 {
    0%, 90%, 100% { transform: translate(0); }
    92% { transform: translate(-2px, -1px); }
    94% { transform: translate(2px, 1px); }
    96% { transform: translate(-1px, 2px); }
  }

  @keyframes glitch2 {
    0%, 90%, 100% { transform: translate(0); }
    91% { transform: translate(2px, 1px); }
    93% { transform: translate(-2px, -1px); }
    95% { transform: translate(1px, -2px); }
  }

  /* ═══════════════════════════════════════════
     RESPONSIVE
  ═══════════════════════════════════════════ */
  @media (max-width: 600px) {
    .analyzer-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
    .metrics-panel { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
    .header-top-bar { font-size: 9px; }
    .badge { font-size: 9px; padding: 3px 8px; }
  }
</style>

  <div class="chat-container">
    <div class="chat-header">
      <div class="chat-header-left">
        <span class="status-dot"></span>
        <span class="chat-header-title">ICA CONVERSATION ENGINE</span>
      </div>
      <span style="font-family:'Share Tech Mono',monospace;font-size:11px;color:var(--text-muted)" id="sessionID">SESSION: INIT</span>
    </div>

    <div class="chat-messages" id="chatMessages">
      <!-- Initial bot message -->
      <div class="message bot">
        <div class="msg-avatar">🤖</div>
        <div>
          <div class="msg-bubble">
            <strong>UM_Authority-Check-Analyzer online.</strong><br><br>
            I am powered by <strong>IBM Bob</strong>, the <strong>ICA conversational engine</strong>, and routed through <strong>MCP Gateway</strong>.<br><br>
            I can diagnose SAP authorization weaknesses across:<br>
            • <strong>ABAP</strong> AUTHORITY-CHECK statements<br>
            • <strong>SU24</strong> authorization proposals<br>
            • <strong>OData</strong> Fiori service paths<br><br>
            ⚠️ This tool is <strong>read-only</strong>. All findings require <strong>SAP Security approval</strong> before any correction is applied.<br><br>
            Select an analyzer above or describe your authorization issue below to begin.
          </div>
          <div class="msg-time" id="initTime"></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="input-area">
      <div class="quick-buttons">
        <button class="quick-btn" onclick="quickAction('Check ABAP program authorization')">⚡ ABAP Check</button>
        <button class="quick-btn" onclick="quickAction('Analyze SU24 proposal for transaction')">📋 SU24 Proposal</button>
        <button class="quick-btn" onclick="quickAction('Scan OData service authorization')">🌐 OData Scan</button>
        <button class="quick-btn" onclick="quickAction('Run combined authorization review')">🔄 Full Audit</button>
        <button class="quick-btn" onclick="quickAction('Show pending findings for approval')">🔔 Pending</button>
      </div>
      <div class="input-row">
        <textarea
          class="input-field"
          id="userInput"
          placeholder="Describe your SAP authorization issue, paste ABAP code, or enter a transaction code..."
          rows="1"
          onkeydown="handleKey(event)"
        ></textarea>
        <button class="send-btn" onclick="sendMessage()" title="Send">➤</button>
      </div>
      <div class="input-footer">ENTER TO SEND · SHIFT+ENTER FOR NEW LINE · ALL DATA PROCESSED LOCALLY</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- AUDIT TRAIL -->
  <div class="audit-panel">
    <div class="audit-header">
      <span class="status-dot"></span>
      AUDIT TRAIL — FULL EVENT LOG
    </div>
    <div class="audit-log" id="auditLog">
      <div class="audit-entry">
        <span class="audit-time" id="auditInitTime"></span>
        <span class="audit-action">[INIT]</span>
        <span class="audit-detail">UM_Authority-Check-Analyzer started · Boundary: READ-ONLY · Gateway: CONNECTED</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- FOOTER -->
  <footer class="footer">
    UM_AUTHORITY-CHECK-ANALYZER  | 
    <span>IBM BOB</span> + <span>ICA ENGINE</span> + <span>MCP GATEWAY</span>
     |  READ-ONLY DIAGNOSTIC  |  HUMAN APPROVAL MANDATORY
  </footer>

</div>

<script>
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
//  UM_Authority-Check-Analyzer — Client Logic
//  Governed SAP Authorization Diagnostic Assistant
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// ── State ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
let selectedAnalyzer = null;
let sessionID        = generateSessionID();
let checksRun        = 0;
let findings         = 0;
let pendingApprovals = 0;
let requestCounter   = 0;

// ── Initialise ─────────────────────────────────────────────
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  const now = new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
  document.getElementById('initTime').textContent = now;
  document.getElementById('auditInitTime').textContent = now;
  document.getElementById('sessionID').textContent = 'SESSION: ' + sessionID;
  updateClock();
  setInterval(updateClock, 1000);
  generateParticles();
  autoResizeTextarea();
});

function generateSessionID() {
  return 'UM-' + Math.random().toString(36).substr(2,4).toUpperCase() + '-' + Date.now().toString(36).toUpperCase();
}

function generateRequestID() {
  requestCounter++;
  return 'REQ-' + String(requestCounter).padStart(4,'0') + '-' + sessionID;
}

function updateClock() {
  document.getElementById('liveTime').textContent = new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
}

// ── Particles ──────────────────────────────────────────────
function generateParticles() {
  const container = document.getElementById('particles');
  for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
    const p = document.createElement('div');
    p.className = 'particle';
    p.style.left = Math.random() * 100 + '%';
    p.style.animationDuration = (8 + Math.random() * 12) + 's';
    p.style.animationDelay = (Math.random() * 10) + 's';
    p.style.setProperty('--drift', (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2);
    p.style.opacity = Math.random() * 0.7;
    const size = 1 + Math.random() * 3;
    p.style.width = size + 'px';
    p.style.height = size + 'px';
    container.appendChild(p);
  }
}

// ── Analyzer selection ─────────────────────────────────────
function selectAnalyzer(type) {
  selectedAnalyzer = type;
  document.querySelectorAll('.analyzer-card').forEach(c => c.classList.remove('active'));
  document.getElementById('card-' + type)?.classList.add('active');
  addAuditEntry('SELECT', 'Analyzer selected: ' + type);
  addBotMessage(
    '🎯 <strong>' + type + ' Analyzer</strong> selected.<br><br>' +
    'Please provide the relevant input:<br>' +
    getAnalyzerPrompt(type)
  );
}

function getAnalyzerPrompt(type) {
  const prompts = {
    ABAP:     '• Paste your ABAP program code, or<br>• Enter the program name (e.g., <code>ZTEST_AUTH</code>), or<br>• Describe the authorization issue you are observing.',
    SU24:     '• Enter the transaction code (e.g., <code>ME21N</code>), or<br>• Paste the SU24 proposal output, or<br>• Describe the missing authorization object.',
    ODATA:    '• Enter the OData service name (e.g., <code>ZMM_PO_SRV</code>), or<br>• Paste the service URL path, or<br>• Describe the Fiori authorization failure.',
    COMBINED: '• Enter one or more transaction codes, or<br>• Paste ABAP code or program names, or<br>• Describe the complete authorization scenario for full audit.'
  };
  return prompts[type] || 'Please describe your authorization issue.';
}

// ── Quick actions ──────────────────────────────────────────
function quickAction(text) {
  document.getElementById('userInput').value = text;
  sendMessage();
}

// ── Send message ───────────────────────────────────────────
function sendMessage() {
  const input = document.getElementById('userInput');
  const text = input.value.trim();
  if (!text) return;

  // Add user message
  addUserMessage(text);
  input.value = '';
  input.style.height = 'auto';

  // Mask sensitive data
  const masked = maskSensitiveData(text);
  if (masked !== text) {
    addBotMessage('🔒 <strong>Privacy Notice:</strong> Sensitive data detected in your input has been masked before processing.');
  }

  // Log to audit
  const reqID = generateRequestID();
  addAuditEntry('USER_INPUT', reqID + ' · Input received · Length: ' + text.length + ' chars');

  // Simulate MCP Gateway check
  showTyping();
  setTimeout(() => {
    hideTyping();
    processInput(masked, reqID);
  }, 1200 + Math.random() * 800);
}

function maskSensitiveData(input) {
  return input
    .replace(/password\s*[:=]\s*\S+/gi, 'password:[MASKED]')
    .replace(/token\s*[:=]\s*\S+/gi, 'token:[MASKED]')
    .replace(/bearer\s+\S+/gi, 'Bearer [MASKED]')
    .replace(/secret\s*[:=]\s*\S+/gi, 'secret:[MASKED]');
}

// ── Process input logic ────────────────────────────────────
function processInput(text, reqID) {
  checksRun++;
  updateMetrics();
  addAuditEntry('MCP_GATEWAY', reqID + ' · Gateway validation: PASSED · Tool: ' + (selectedAnalyzer || 'AUTO') + '_ANALYZER');

  const lower = text.toLowerCase();

  if (lower.includes('authority-check') || lower.includes('abap') || selectedAnalyzer === 'ABAP') {
    runABAPAnalysis(text, reqID);
  } else if (lower.includes('su24') || lower.includes('proposal') || selectedAnalyzer === 'SU24') {
    runSU24Analysis(text, reqID);
  } else if (lower.includes('odata') || lower.includes('fiori') || lower.includes('srv') || selectedAnalyzer === 'ODATA') {
    runODataAnalysis(text, reqID);
  } else if (lower.includes('combined') || lower.includes('full audit') || selectedAnalyzer === 'COMBINED') {
    runCombinedAnalysis(text, reqID);
  } else if (lower.includes('pending')) {
    showPendingFindings(reqID);
  } else {
    addBotMessage(
      '🔍 <strong>ICA Engine</strong> routing your request through MCP Gateway...<br><br>' +
      'Request ID: <code>' + reqID + '</code><br><br>' +
      'Please select a specific analyzer above, or clarify your request:<br><br>' +
      '• <strong>ABAP</strong> — for AUTHORITY-CHECK code analysis<br>' +
      '• <strong>SU24</strong> — for authorization proposal review<br>' +
      '• <strong>OData</strong> — for Fiori service authorization<br>' +
      '• <strong>Combined</strong> — for comprehensive audit'
    );
    addAuditEntry('ROUTING', reqID + ' · Analyzer auto-detect: INCONCLUSIVE · Awaiting clarification');
  }
}

// ── ABAP Analysis ──────────────────────────────────────────
function runABAPAnalysis(text, reqID) {
  addAuditEntry('ABAP_ANALYZER', reqID + ' · ABAP analysis initiated · Read-only boundary: ENFORCED');

  const msgEl = addBotMessage(
    '🔍 <strong>ABAP Analyzer</strong> processing via IBM Bob...<br><br>' +
    'Request ID: <code>' + reqID + '</code><br>' +
    'Boundary: <code>READ-ONLY</code><br>' +
    'Scanning AUTHORITY-CHECK statements and authorization objects...'
  );

  setTimeout(() => {
    findings++;
    pendingApprovals++;
    updateMetrics();
    addFindingCard({
      id:         reqID + '-F001',
      checker:    '🔍 ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK ANALYZER',
      severity:   'HIGH',
      status:     '⚠️ FINDING DETECTED',
      transaction: 'ZTEST_PROG',
      confidence: '94%',
      title:      'AUTHORITY-CHECK using S_TCODE without CHECK OBJECT complement — Bypass risk identified.',
      evidence:   'Line 47: AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT \'S_TCODE\' ID \'TCD\' FIELD sy-tcode.\nMissing complementary object check for S_DEVELOP or object-specific authority.',
      correction: 'Add S_DEVELOP check with OBJTYPE and OBJNAME constraints. Engage SAP Security team for role adjustment.'
    });
    addAuditEntry('FINDING', reqID + '-F001 · Severity: HIGH · Status: PENDING_APPROVAL · Human approval required');
    addBotMessage(
      '✅ <strong>ABAP Analysis Complete</strong> — Request ID: <code>' + reqID + '</code><br><br>' +
      '1 finding identified. The finding card above requires <strong>SAP Security approval</strong> before any correction is applied.'
    );
  }, 1500);
}

// ── SU24 Analysis ──────────────────────────────────────────
function runSU24Analysis(text, reqID) {
  addAuditEntry('SU24_ANALYZER', reqID + ' · SU24 analysis initiated · Read-only boundary: ENFORCED');
  addBotMessage(
    '📋 <strong>SU24 Analyzer</strong> processing via IBM Bob...<br><br>' +
    'Request ID: <code>' + reqID + '</code><br>' +
    'Analyzing authorization proposal objects and transaction mappings...'
  );
  setTimeout(() => {
    findings += 2;
    pendingApprovals += 2;
    updateMetrics();
    addFindingCard({
      id:         reqID + '-F002',
      checker:    '📋 SU24 PROPOSAL ANALYZER',
      severity:   'CRITICAL',
      status:     '🚨 CRITICAL FINDING',
      transaction: 'ME21N',
      confidence: '98%',
      title:      'Authorization object M_BEST_BSA missing from SU24 proposal for ME21N — Purchase order creation unprotected.',
      evidence:   'SU24 check: M_BEST_BSA (Document type) → NOT FOUND in proposal table USOBT_C for program SAPMM06E.',
      correction: 'Add M_BEST_BSA with ACTVT=01 and BSART=* to SU24 proposal. Regenerate role using PFCG after security approval.'
    });
    addFindingCard({
      id:         reqID + '-F003',
      checker:    '📋 SU24 PROPOSAL ANALYZER',
      severity:   'MEDIUM',
      status:     '⚠️ ADVISORY',
      transaction: 'ME23N',
      confidence: '81%',
      title:      'M_BEST_WRK proposal marked CM (check maintained) but activity 03 only — Display scope incomplete.',
      evidence:   'SU24 table USOBT_C: M_BEST_WRK · ACTVT=03 only. Activity 02 (change) and 01 (create) not covered.',
      correction: 'Review business requirement. Add ACTVT 01,02 if ME23N must support change scenario in this role.'
    });
    addAuditEntry('FINDING', reqID + '-F002 · CRITICAL · PENDING_APPROVAL');
    addAuditEntry('FINDING', reqID + '-F003 · MEDIUM · PENDING_APPROVAL');
    addBotMessage(
      '✅ <strong>SU24 Analysis Complete</strong> — 2 findings identified.<br><br>' +
      '⚠️ 1 CRITICAL finding requires <strong>immediate SAP Security review</strong>.'
    );
  }, 1500);
}

// ── OData Analysis ─────────────────────────────────────────
function runODataAnalysis(text, reqID) {
  addAuditEntry('ODATA_ANALYZER', reqID + ' · OData analysis initiated · Read-only boundary: ENFORCED');
  addBotMessage(
    '🌐 <strong>OData Analyzer</strong> processing via IBM Bob...<br><br>' +
    'Request ID: <code>' + reqID + '</code><br>' +
    'Scanning Fiori service paths and entity set authorization objects...'
  );
  setTimeout(() => {
    findings++;
    pendingApprovals++;
    updateMetrics();
    addFindingCard({
      id:         reqID + '-F004',
      checker:    '🌐 ODATA SERVICE ANALYZER',
      severity:   'HIGH',
      status:     '⚠️ FINDING DETECTED',
      transaction: 'ZMM_PO_SRV',
      confidence: '91%',
      title:      'OData service ZMM_PO_SRV EntitySet PurchaseOrderSet missing S_SERVICE authorization check.',
      evidence:   'ICF node: /sap/opu/odata/sap/ZMM_PO_SRV\nService check table: SACF_AS → S_SERVICE object not registered for ZPOREAD function group.',
      correction: 'Register S_SERVICE object for ZMM_PO_SRV in transaction SICF and SOAMANAGER. Assign to Fiori role via PFCG.'
    });
    addAuditEntry('FINDING', reqID + '-F004 · HIGH · PENDING_APPROVAL');
    addBotMessage(
      '✅ <strong>OData Analysis Complete</strong> — 1 finding identified. Human approval required before remediation.'
    );
  }, 1500);
}

// ── Combined Analysis ──────────────────────────────────────
function runCombinedAnalysis(text, reqID) {
  addAuditEntry('COMBINED_ANALYZER', reqID + ' · All three analyzers initiated · READ-ONLY · COMBINED MODE');
  addBotMessage(
    '📊 <strong>Combined Review</strong> — All three analyzers activated...<br><br>' +
    'Request ID: <code>' + reqID + '</code><br>' +
    '• ABAP Analyzer → Active<br>' +
    '• SU24 Analyzer → Active<br>' +
    '• OData Analyzer → Active<br><br>' +
    'Processing through IBM Bob via MCP Gateway...'
  );
  setTimeout(() => { runABAPAnalysis(text, reqID + '-ABAP'); }, 800);
  setTimeout(() => { runSU24Analysis(text, reqID + '-SU24'); }, 2000);
  setTimeout(() => { runODataAnalysis(text, reqID + '-ODA'); }, 3200);
}

// ── Pending findings ───────────────────────────────────────
function showPendingFindings(reqID) {
  addBotMessage(
    '🔔 <strong>Pending Approvals Dashboard</strong><br><br>' +
    'Pending items: <code>' + pendingApprovals + '</code><br>' +
    'Total findings this session: <code>' + findings + '</code><br>' +
    'Total checks run: <code>' + checksRun + '</code><br><br>' +
    '⚠️ All pending findings require <strong>SAP Security team approval</strong> before any correction can be applied.'
  );
  addAuditEntry('QUERY', reqID + ' · Pending findings queried · Count: ' + pendingApprovals);
}

// ── UI Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────
function addUserMessage(text) {
  const chat = document.getElementById('chatMessages');
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.className = 'message user';
  div.innerHTML = `
    <div class="msg-avatar">👤</div>
    <div>
      <div class="msg-bubble">${escapeHTML(text)}</div>
      <div class="msg-time">${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}</div>
    </div>`;
  chat.appendChild(div);
  scrollChat();
}

function addBotMessage(html) {
  const chat = document.getElementById('chatMessages');
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.className = 'message bot';
  div.innerHTML = `
    <div class="msg-avatar">🤖</div>
    <div>
      <div class="msg-bubble">${html}</div>
      <div class="msg-time">${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}</div>
    </div>`;
  chat.appendChild(div);
  scrollChat();
  return div;
}

function addFindingCard(f) {
  const chat = document.getElementById('chatMessages');
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.className = 'message bot';
  const sClass = 'severity-' + f.severity.toLowerCase();
  div.innerHTML = `
    <div class="msg-avatar">🚨</div>
    <div style="flex:1">
      <div class="finding-card">
        <span class="finding-severity ${sClass}">${f.severity}</span>
        <div class="finding-title">${f.checker}</div>
        <div class="finding-detail" style="margin-bottom:8px">
          <strong style="color:var(--neon-red)">Finding ID:</strong> <code>${f.id}</code>  
          <strong style="color:var(--neon-red)">Confidence:</strong> ${f.confidence}<br>
          <strong style="color:var(--neon-red)">Transaction:</strong> ${f.transaction}
        </div>
        <div class="finding-detail">
          <strong>⚠️ Finding:</strong><br>${f.title}
        </div>
        <pre>${f.evidence}</pre>
        <div class="finding-detail">
          <strong>💡 Recommended Correction:</strong><br>${f.correction}
        </div>
        <div class="finding-detail" style="margin-top:10px;padding:8px;background:rgba(255,0,51,0.05);border:1px solid rgba(255,0,51,0.2);border-radius:4px;">
          ⚠️ <strong style="color:var(--neon-red)">Human approval mandatory</strong> before any correction is applied.
        </div>
        <div class="finding-action-row">
          <button class="action-btn btn-approve" onclick="handleAction('APPROVE','${f.id}')">✅ APPROVE</button>
          <button class="action-btn btn-reject" onclick="handleAction('REJECT','${f.id}')">❌ REJECT</button>
          <button class="action-btn btn-evidence" onclick="handleAction('EVIDENCE','${f.id}')">🔍 MORE EVIDENCE</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="msg-time">${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}</div>
    </div>`;
  chat.appendChild(div);
  scrollChat();
}

function handleAction(action, findingID) {
  if (action === 'APPROVE') {
    pendingApprovals = Math.max(0, pendingApprovals - 1);
    updateMetrics();
    addBotMessage(
      '✅ <strong>Finding ' + findingID + ' APPROVED</strong><br><br>' +
      'Human approval recorded. The correction workflow can now proceed through the SAP Security change management process.'
    );
    addAuditEntry('APPROVE', findingID + ' · Approved by user · Correction workflow authorized');
  } else if (action === 'REJECT') {
    pendingApprovals = Math.max(0, pendingApprovals - 1);
    updateMetrics();
    addBotMessage(
      '❌ <strong>Finding ' + findingID + ' REJECTED</strong><br><br>' +
      'Finding has been marked as rejected. No correction will be applied. This decision is logged in the audit trail.'
    );
    addAuditEntry('REJECT', findingID + ' · Rejected by user · No action to be taken');
  } else {
    addBotMessage(
      '🔍 <strong>Additional Evidence Requested</strong> for Finding ' + findingID + '<br><br>' +
      'Please provide:<br>• Additional transaction context<br>• Role name and user assignment<br>• System trace output (ST05 or SU53)'
    );
    addAuditEntry('EVIDENCE_REQUEST', findingID + ' · Additional evidence requested');
  }
}

function showTyping() {
  const chat = document.getElementById('chatMessages');
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.className = 'message bot';
  div.id = 'typingIndicator';
  div.innerHTML = `
    <div class="msg-avatar">🤖</div>
    <div class="msg-bubble" style="padding:8px 16px">
      <div class="typing-indicator">
        <div class="typing-dot"></div>
        <div class="typing-dot"></div>
        <div class="typing-dot"></div>
        <span style="font-family:'Share Tech Mono',monospace;font-size:11px;color:var(--text-muted);margin-left:8px">IBM Bob processing via MCP Gateway...</span>
      </div>
    </div>`;
  chat.appendChild(div);
  scrollChat();
}

function hideTyping() {
  const el = document.getElementById('typingIndicator');
  if (el) el.remove();
}

function addAuditEntry(action, detail) {
  const log = document.getElementById('auditLog');
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.className = 'audit-entry';
  div.innerHTML = `
    <span class="audit-time">${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}</span>
    <span class="audit-action">[${action}]</span>
    <span class="audit-detail">${detail}</span>`;
  log.appendChild(div);
  log.scrollTop = log.scrollHeight;
}

function updateMetrics() {
  document.getElementById('mChecks').textContent   = checksRun;
  document.getElementById('mFindings').textContent  = findings;
  document.getElementById('mPending').textContent   = pendingApprovals;
}

function scrollChat() {
  const chat = document.getElementById('chatMessages');
  chat.scrollTop = chat.scrollHeight;
}

function escapeHTML(str) {
  return str
    .replace(/&/g,'&')
    .replace(/</g,'<')
    .replace(/>/g,'>')
    .replace(/"/g,'"');
}

function handleKey(e) {
  if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) {
    e.preventDefault();
    sendMessage();
  }
}

function autoResizeTextarea() {
  const ta = document.getElementById('userInput');
  ta.addEventListener('input', () => {
    ta.style.height = 'auto';
    ta.style.height = Math.min(ta.scrollHeight, 150) + 'px';
  });
}
</script>
</body>
</html>

# 1. What problem does this solution solve?
In a normal SAP project, a consultant or developer may have to manually inspect code, transaction proposals and OData services to answer a simple question: "Can this business action be performed safely, and are the required authorization checks present?" The work can take time, and the final explanation may depend on the experience of the person doing the review.

### What proves that the step is complete
 Unit tests for present, missing, misplaced and unreachable checks.

# SAP Authorization Check Automation with IBM BOB + ICA

Yes, this can absolutely be done! The solution is well-documented as a governed implementation model that automates SAP authorization reviews using IBM Bob, ICA (conversational assistant), and an MCP Gateway. Here's a detailed step-by-step guide:

---

## 🔍 What Problem Does This Solve?

In a normal SAP project, consultants or developers must manually inspect code, transaction proposals, and OData services to answer: *"Can this business action be performed safely, and are the required authorization checks present?"* This is time-consuming and depends heavily on individual expertise [1].

---

## 🏗️ How the Solution Works — Core Components

The solution has three main components working together [1]:

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| **ICA** | The conversational chat layer — collects inputs, asks clarifying questions, explains findings in simple language |
| **MCP Gateway** | The controlled door — authenticates requests, enforces allow-lists, validates tokens, logs all calls |
| **IBM Bob** | The orchestration coordinator — selects only approved tools and coordinates the three security analyzers |

---

## 🔬 The Three Security Analyzers

### A. ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
- Finds missing, weak, misplaced, or unreachable `AUTHORITY-CHECK` statements
- Points to the **exact code line** causing the finding
- Suggests corrected patterns with confidence scoring [1]

> *Example question: "Does this program check whether the user may change the company code before saving the document?"*

### B. SU24 Analyzer
- Compares transaction and authorization default proposals
- Detects **missing or excessive** authorization proposals
- Recommends maintainable SU24 corrections [1]

### C. OData Authorization Analyzer
- Follows the full service path: service → entity → operation → implementation → authorization decision
- Identifies gaps between "technically reachable" and "properly protected"
- Checks service activation, entity sets, DPC/DPC_EXT, authorization mapping, and gateway exposure [1]

> *Example question: "Can this Fiori service read or change data without checking the user's company code or business role?"*

---

## 📋 Step-by-Step Implementation Plan

### ✅ Step 1: Define Scope and Success Criteria
- Approve the **three initial surfaces**: ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK, SU24 proposals, and OData authorization entry points
- Define success in measurable terms: correct finding location, understandable explanation, no unauthorized writes, complete audit record, and acceptable response time
- Deliverables needed:
  - Signed scope statement
  - Approved list of inputs and outputs
  - Out-of-scope register
  - Acceptance criteria agreed by SAP Security, SAP Development, and Change Management [1]

**Primary Owner:** SAP Security Architect with Business and AI Platform owners

---

### ✅ Step 2: Prepare Secure Inputs
Create a **standard intake package** so the assistant receives complete, comparable information every time [1]:

- Create an intake form with: Request ID, requester, project, system type, SAP release, client, business process, and change ticket
- **For ABAP:** Accept controlled file or repository reference, program/object name, package, and relevant include names *(no executable files)*
- **For SU24:** Capture transaction name, intended business action, expected authorization objects, and existing proposal evidence
- **For OData:** Capture service name, version, entity set, operation, application/tile, implementation reference, and test evidence
- Add a **privacy step** to remove passwords, tokens, personal identifiers, and customer data
- Assign a unique **Request ID** and calculate an input hash for traceability

**Primary Owner:** SAP Security and AI Platform teams

---

### ✅ Step 3: Register Approved Tools in the MCP Gateway
The gateway is the guarded entrance — ICA and Bob must never call raw tools directly [1]:

- Register only the three approved analyzers in the tool catalogue
- Configure authentication, token validation, and rate limits
- Enforce the allow-list so unauthorized tools are automatically rejected
- Enable full request logging (request ID, user, tool, result status)

**Proof of completion:**
- Tool catalogue showing approved status
- Successful schema validation test
- Rejected unauthorized-tool test
- Gateway logs verified [1]

**Primary Owner:** AI Platform / MCP Gateway owner

---

### ✅ Step 4: Configure IBM Bob as the Governed Orchestrator
Bob coordinates the work — he must not invent new checks or bypass the gateway [1]:

- Configure Bob to select **only approved tools**
- Restrict Bob to the approved three-checker scope
- Define normalized input/output schemas (versioned)
- Set stop conditions: Bob stops if evidence is insufficient or if a write operation is attempted
- Review all prompts/instructions with SAP Security

**Primary Owner:** IBM Bob product owner with SAP Security approver

---

### ✅ Step 5: Build the ICA Conversational Assistant
ICA makes the technical engine usable without requiring deep technical knowledge [1]:

- Create a **welcome message** explaining what the assistant can inspect and what it cannot change
- Ask questions in logical order: objective → system → release → business action → source evidence → analysis type → change ticket
- Use simple choices: ABAP, SU24, OData, or combined review
- Show a **confirmation screen** before analysis:
  > *"You are asking us to inspect X in system Y using evidence Z. Continue?"*
- Produce readable reports with sanitized real samples

**Primary Owner:** ICA experience owner

---

### ✅ Step 6: Implement the ABAP Analyzer
This component identifies exactly where authorization weaknesses exist [1]:

- Parse ABAP source as **text to inspect, not code to execute**
- Identify authorization-relevant statements, objects, fields, values, branches, loops, exits, and calls to related routines
- Check whether:
  - The `AUTHORITY-CHECK` exists
  - It is reachable in the code path
  - The result is actually evaluated
  - The checked fields match the business action
- Produce line-level evidence with each finding

**Proof of completion:**
- Unit tests for present, missing, misplaced, and unreachable checks
- Line-level evidence test
- False-positive review by ABAP and SAP Security expert [1]

**Primary Owner:** ABAP Engineering owner with SAP Security

---

### ✅ Step 7: Implement the SU24 Analyzer
This component validates that authorization proposals support the intended transaction design [1]:

- Compare transaction/application against existing SU24 proposals
- Detect missing, excessive, or inconsistent authorization object entries
- Explain the business impact of each gap
- Recommend maintainable SU24 corrections

**Proof of completion:**
- Positive and negative SU24 samples tested
- Object and field comparison test passed
- Broad-access warning test passed
- Recommendation reviewed by SAP Security and Basis/Development [1]

**Primary Owner:** SAP Security / GRC owner

---

### ✅ Step 8: Implement the OData Authorization Analyzer
This component follows the full service path to verify protection of exposed business operations [1]:

- Check service activation, entity set, operation, DPC/DPC_EXT or behavior implementation
- Verify authorization mapping and gateway exposure
- Identify gaps between technical accessibility and proper authorization protection
- Test read operations, change operations, unauthorized user scenarios, and organizational-value filtering

**Primary Owner:** SAP Fiori / Gateway / SAP Security owner

---

### ✅ Step 9: Build Evidence, Findings, and Reporting
A report is trustworthy only when another person can understand how the conclusion was reached [1].

Each finding record must include:
- **Technical evidence** (exact code line or configuration)
- **Risk classification** and severity
- **Confidence level** and limitations
- **Mitigation/correction** guidance with normalized code samples
- **Remediation steps**
- Link to human security approval and transport/change record

**Approval states to define:**
Draft → Analyzed → Needs Evidence → Security Review → Development Review → Change Submitted → Retest Passed → Closed/Rejected [1]

---

### ✅ Step 10: Connect SAP Evidence Sources Safely
Connect only the evidence that is needed — keep the first version **read-only** [1]:

- Build a connection inventory
- Prove read-only access for all connections
- Implement secret rotation and expiry
- Separate environments (dev/test/prod)
- Maintain evidence retrieval audit records

**Primary Owner:** SAP Platform / Basis and AI Platform teams

---

### ✅ Step 11: Apply Security, Privacy, and Operational Guardrails
The system must enforce these guardrails at all times [1]:

| Guardrail | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Read-only by default** | No automatic changes to SAP systems |
| **Least privilege** | Minimum access required for analysis only |
| **No automatic production change** | All changes go through human approval |
| **Human approval mandatory** | A qualified person must approve every finding |
| **Sensitive data masking** | Passwords, tokens, and personal data are masked |
| **Full audit trail** | Every action is logged and traceable |
| **Confidence and limitations shown** | No hidden uncertainty in findings |

---

### ✅ Step 12: Test with Safe Samples

Run the full test pack [1]:

| Test ID | Scenario | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|
| T01 | Valid ABAP with correct authorization check | Pass/informational with evidence |
| T02 | ABAP with missing check before sensitive operation | Finding points to exact line with correction |
| T03 | ABAP check exists only in unreachable branch | Finding explains reachability concern |
| T04 | SU24 proposal is missing | Identifies transaction/object/field with safe correction |
| T05 | SU24 proposal is too broad | Warning separates proposal issue from role-design issue |

Also run: integration testing (ICA → Gateway → Bob → Analyzer → Report), security testing, and user acceptance testing.

---

### ✅ Step 13: Human Approval, Pilot, and Scale

1. **Human approval** — SAP Security reviews and approves all findings before any change
2. **Pilot** — Run with a small, controlled set of real but safe samples
3. **Scale** — Expand scope gradually with continuous improvement [1]

---

## ⚠️ Important Safety Boundaries

The solution is **NOT** [1]:
- A replacement for SAP Security, Development, or Change Management
- Allowed to automatically grant access or fix production systems
- Allowed to guess when evidence is missing — it must say *"not enough evidence"* and request more
- Allowed to hide uncertainty — every conclusion must show supporting evidence and its limitations

---

## 👥 Role Ownership Summary

| Role | Owns |
|---|---|
| Business Owner | Business context, priority, and acceptance |
| SAP Security | Rules, severity, authorization interpretation, and security approval |
| AI Platform | Operates ICA, MCP Gateway, and IBM Bob |
| SAP Development | Applies corrections and provides evidence |
| Change Management | Manages transport and change records |
| Audit | Independent review and compliance assurance [1] |

---

## 🏁 Definition of Done

The implementation is ready for controlled adoption only when [1]:
> The scope is approved; inputs are classified and masked; schemas are versioned; tools are allow-listed; Bob and ICA stop safely; all three analyzers provide evidence-backed results; production write operations are blocked; human approval and change records are connected; pilot results are accepted; monitoring, support, and audit procedures are documented.

---

This is a well-structured, governable, and implementable solution. The key to success is starting with a **narrow scope**, enforcing **human approval at every stage**, and building confidence gradually before scaling. Would you like me to dive deeper into any specific step?

# SAP Authorization Check Automation with IBM BOB + ICA

Yes, this can absolutely be done! The solution is well-documented as a governed implementation model that automates SAP authorization reviews using IBM Bob, ICA (conversational assistant), and an MCP Gateway. Here's a detailed step-by-step guide:

---

## 🔍 What Problem Does This Solve?

In a normal SAP project, consultants or developers must manually inspect code, transaction proposals, and OData services to answer: *"Can this business action be performed safely, and are the required authorization checks present?"* This is time-consuming and depends heavily on individual expertise [1].

---

## 🏗️ How the Solution Works — Core Components

The solution has three main components working together [1]:

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| **ICA** | The conversational chat layer — collects inputs, asks clarifying questions, explains findings in simple language |
| **MCP Gateway** | The controlled door — authenticates requests, enforces allow-lists, validates tokens, logs all calls |
| **IBM Bob** | The orchestration coordinator — selects only approved tools and coordinates the three security analyzers |

---

## 🔬 The Three Security Analyzers

### A. ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
- Finds missing, weak, misplaced, or unreachable `AUTHORITY-CHECK` statements
- Points to the **exact code line** causing the finding
- Suggests corrected patterns with confidence scoring [1]

> *Example question: "Does this program check whether the user may change the company code before saving the document?"*

### B. SU24 Analyzer
- Compares transaction and authorization default proposals
- Detects **missing or excessive** authorization proposals
- Recommends maintainable SU24 corrections [1]

### C. OData Authorization Analyzer
- Follows the full service path: service → entity → operation → implementation → authorization decision
- Identifies gaps between "technically reachable" and "properly protected"
- Checks service activation, entity sets, DPC/DPC_EXT, authorization mapping, and gateway exposure [1]

> *Example question: "Can this Fiori service read or change data without checking the user's company code or business role?"*

---

## 📋 Step-by-Step Implementation Plan

### ✅ Step 1: Define Scope and Success Criteria
- Approve the **three initial surfaces**: ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK, SU24 proposals, and OData authorization entry points
- Define success in measurable terms: correct finding location, understandable explanation, no unauthorized writes, complete audit record, and acceptable response time
- Deliverables needed:
  - Signed scope statement
  - Approved list of inputs and outputs
  - Out-of-scope register
  - Acceptance criteria agreed by SAP Security, SAP Development, and Change Management [1]

**Primary Owner:** SAP Security Architect with Business and AI Platform owners

---

### ✅ Step 2: Prepare Secure Inputs
Create a **standard intake package** so the assistant receives complete, comparable information every time [1]:

- Create an intake form with: Request ID, requester, project, system type, SAP release, client, business process, and change ticket
- **For ABAP:** Accept controlled file or repository reference, program/object name, package, and relevant include names *(no executable files)*
- **For SU24:** Capture transaction name, intended business action, expected authorization objects, and existing proposal evidence
- **For OData:** Capture service name, version, entity set, operation, application/tile, implementation reference, and test evidence
- Add a **privacy step** to remove passwords, tokens, personal identifiers, and customer data
- Assign a unique **Request ID** and calculate an input hash for traceability

**Primary Owner:** SAP Security and AI Platform teams

---

### ✅ Step 3: Register Approved Tools in the MCP Gateway
The gateway is the guarded entrance — ICA and Bob must never call raw tools directly [1]:

- Register only the three approved analyzers in the tool catalogue
- Configure authentication, token validation, and rate limits
- Enforce the allow-list so unauthorized tools are automatically rejected
- Enable full request logging (request ID, user, tool, result status)

**Proof of completion:**
- Tool catalogue showing approved status
- Successful schema validation test
- Rejected unauthorized-tool test
- Gateway logs verified [1]

**Primary Owner:** AI Platform / MCP Gateway owner

---

### ✅ Step 4: Configure IBM Bob as the Governed Orchestrator
Bob coordinates the work — he must not invent new checks or bypass the gateway [1]:

- Configure Bob to select **only approved tools**
- Restrict Bob to the approved three-checker scope
- Define normalized input/output schemas (versioned)
- Set stop conditions: Bob stops if evidence is insufficient or if a write operation is attempted
- Review all prompts/instructions with SAP Security

**Primary Owner:** IBM Bob product owner with SAP Security approver

---

### ✅ Step 5: Build the ICA Conversational Assistant
ICA makes the technical engine usable without requiring deep technical knowledge [1]:

- Create a **welcome message** explaining what the assistant can inspect and what it cannot change
- Ask questions in logical order: objective → system → release → business action → source evidence → analysis type → change ticket
- Use simple choices: ABAP, SU24, OData, or combined review
- Show a **confirmation screen** before analysis:
  > *"You are asking us to inspect X in system Y using evidence Z. Continue?"*
- Produce readable reports with sanitized real samples

**Primary Owner:** ICA experience owner

---

### ✅ Step 6: Implement the ABAP Analyzer
This component identifies exactly where authorization weaknesses exist [1]:

- Parse ABAP source as **text to inspect, not code to execute**
- Identify authorization-relevant statements, objects, fields, values, branches, loops, exits, and calls to related routines
- Check whether:
  - The `AUTHORITY-CHECK` exists
  - It is reachable in the code path
  - The result is actually evaluated
  - The checked fields match the business action
- Produce line-level evidence with each finding

**Proof of completion:**
- Unit tests for present, missing, misplaced, and unreachable checks
- Line-level evidence test
- False-positive review by ABAP and SAP Security expert [1]

**Primary Owner:** ABAP Engineering owner with SAP Security

---

### ✅ Step 7: Implement the SU24 Analyzer
This component validates that authorization proposals support the intended transaction design [1]:

- Compare transaction/application against existing SU24 proposals
- Detect missing, excessive, or inconsistent authorization object entries
- Explain the business impact of each gap
- Recommend maintainable SU24 corrections

**Proof of completion:**
- Positive and negative SU24 samples tested
- Object and field comparison test passed
- Broad-access warning test passed
- Recommendation reviewed by SAP Security and Basis/Development [1]

**Primary Owner:** SAP Security / GRC owner

---

### ✅ Step 8: Implement the OData Authorization Analyzer
This component follows the full service path to verify protection of exposed business operations [1]:

- Check service activation, entity set, operation, DPC/DPC_EXT or behavior implementation
- Verify authorization mapping and gateway exposure
- Identify gaps between technical accessibility and proper authorization protection
- Test read operations, change operations, unauthorized user scenarios, and organizational-value filtering

**Primary Owner:** SAP Fiori / Gateway / SAP Security owner

---

### ✅ Step 9: Build Evidence, Findings, and Reporting
A report is trustworthy only when another person can understand how the conclusion was reached [1].

Each finding record must include:
- **Technical evidence** (exact code line or configuration)
- **Risk classification** and severity
- **Confidence level** and limitations
- **Mitigation/correction** guidance with normalized code samples
- **Remediation steps**
- Link to human security approval and transport/change record

**Approval states to define:**
Draft → Analyzed → Needs Evidence → Security Review → Development Review → Change Submitted → Retest Passed → Closed/Rejected [1]

---

### ✅ Step 10: Connect SAP Evidence Sources Safely
Connect only the evidence that is needed — keep the first version **read-only** [1]:

- Build a connection inventory
- Prove read-only access for all connections
- Implement secret rotation and expiry
- Separate environments (dev/test/prod)
- Maintain evidence retrieval audit records

**Primary Owner:** SAP Platform / Basis and AI Platform teams

---

### ✅ Step 11: Apply Security, Privacy, and Operational Guardrails
The system must enforce these guardrails at all times [1]:

| Guardrail | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Read-only by default** | No automatic changes to SAP systems |
| **Least privilege** | Minimum access required for analysis only |
| **No automatic production change** | All changes go through human approval |
| **Human approval mandatory** | A qualified person must approve every finding |
| **Sensitive data masking** | Passwords, tokens, and personal data are masked |
| **Full audit trail** | Every action is logged and traceable |
| **Confidence and limitations shown** | No hidden uncertainty in findings |

---

### ✅ Step 12: Test with Safe Samples

Run the full test pack [1]:

| Test ID | Scenario | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|
| T01 | Valid ABAP with correct authorization check | Pass/informational with evidence |
| T02 | ABAP with missing check before sensitive operation | Finding points to exact line with correction |
| T03 | ABAP check exists only in unreachable branch | Finding explains reachability concern |
| T04 | SU24 proposal is missing | Identifies transaction/object/field with safe correction |
| T05 | SU24 proposal is too broad | Warning separates proposal issue from role-design issue |

Also run: integration testing (ICA → Gateway → Bob → Analyzer → Report), security testing, and user acceptance testing.

---

### ✅ Step 13: Human Approval, Pilot, and Scale

1. **Human approval** — SAP Security reviews and approves all findings before any change
2. **Pilot** — Run with a small, controlled set of real but safe samples
3. **Scale** — Expand scope gradually with continuous improvement [1]

---

## ⚠️ Important Safety Boundaries

The solution is **NOT** [1]:
- A replacement for SAP Security, Development, or Change Management
- Allowed to automatically grant access or fix production systems
- Allowed to guess when evidence is missing — it must say *"not enough evidence"* and request more
- Allowed to hide uncertainty — every conclusion must show supporting evidence and its limitations

---

## 👥 Role Ownership Summary

| Role | Owns |
|---|---|
| Business Owner | Business context, priority, and acceptance |
| SAP Security | Rules, severity, authorization interpretation, and security approval |
| AI Platform | Operates ICA, MCP Gateway, and IBM Bob |
| SAP Development | Applies corrections and provides evidence |
| Change Management | Manages transport and change records |
| Audit | Independent review and compliance assurance [1] |

---

## 🏁 Definition of Done

The implementation is ready for controlled adoption only when [1]:
> The scope is approved; inputs are classified and masked; schemas are versioned; tools are allow-listed; Bob and ICA stop safely; all three analyzers provide evidence-backed results; production write operations are blocked; human approval and change records are connected; pilot results are accepted; monitoring, support, and audit procedures are documented.

---

This is a well-structured, governable, and implementable solution. The key to success is starting with a **narrow scope**, enforcing **human approval at every stage**, and building confidence gradually before scaling. Would you like me to dive deeper into any specific step?

# MCP Gateway: Tools & Technology Recommendations

Based on the implementation guide and current MCP Gateway landscape, here is a comprehensive breakdown of your options.

---

## 🏗️ What the MCP Gateway Must Do (Requirements First)

Before choosing a tool, the gateway in this SAP Authorization solution must handle these specific responsibilities [2]:

| Responsibility | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Authentication** | Validate tokens before any tool is called |
| **Allow-list enforcement** | Only the 3 approved analyzers may be called |
| **Rate limiting** | Prevent abuse and runaway calls |
| **Full request logging** | Log Request ID, user, tool, and result status |
| **Failure safety** | If validation fails → stop the request, never guess |
| **Tool versioning** | Record tool versions so reports can be compared over time |
| **Read-only enforcement** | Block any production write attempt automatically |

---

## 🌐 Open-Source MCP Gateway Options

### 1. 🥇 Lunar.dev Open Source MCP Gateway
- Sits between AI agents and MCP servers [1]
- Centralizes authentication, enforces access control, and logs every tool invocation
- Strong fit for the **allow-list + logging** requirements in this solution
- **Best for:** Teams wanting full control over their gateway infrastructure

### 2. AWS Labs MCP (Open Source)
- Available on GitHub (`awslabs/mcp`) [1]
- Includes direct resource management with security scanning and best practices
- Has an **AWS Systems Manager for SAP MCP Server** — directly relevant for SAP landscapes
- **Best for:** AWS-hosted SAP environments

### 3. MCP Protocol Native Framework (Anthropic)
- The Model Context Protocol itself is an **open standard and open-source framework** introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 [1]
- Provides the universal integration layer between AI systems and tools/data sources
- Acts as the foundational protocol on top of which any gateway can be built
- **Best for:** Building a custom, lightweight gateway from scratch

---

## 💼 Commercial MCP Gateway Options

### 4. SAP Integration Suite — MCP Gateway ⭐ *(Most Relevant)*
- SAP's own reference architecture explicitly supports **"MCP Gateway in SAP Integration Suite"** for exposing SAP and non-SAP APIs as a unified MCP tool catalog [1]
- Microsoft Copilot Studio agents authenticate to this gateway using **OAuth 2.0 Authorization** [1]
- **Best for:** SAP-centric environments — this is the most native fit for this solution

### 5. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
- Supports **OpenAPI targets (REST APIs)** with multiple authentication methods [1]
- Enterprise-grade managed service
- **Best for:** AWS-native deployments using Amazon Bedrock as the AI backbone

### 6. Azure API Management (APIM) with MCP Support
- Features **Azure AD/Entra ID native authentication** [1]
- Choice between open-source Kubernetes gateway and managed APIM option [1]
- **Best for:** Azure-centric enterprise environments with Microsoft identity infrastructure

### 7. Lasso Security-First MCP Gateway
- Features **PII masking with Presidio integration** — detects and redacts sensitive data automatically [1]
- Available as both Open-Source and Commercial deployment [1]
- **Best for:** Environments with strict data privacy requirements (aligns with the sensitive data masking guardrail) [2]

### 8. MuleSoft Omni Gateway (Flex Gateway)
- Envoy-based, ultrafast lightweight API gateway [1]
- Designed to manage and secure APIs running anywhere
- **Best for:** Organizations already using MuleSoft for SAP integration

---

## 🎯 Recommendation Matrix for This SAP Solution

| Scenario | Recommended Gateway |
|---|---|
| SAP-native, on-premise or BTP | **SAP Integration Suite MCP Gateway** |
| AWS-hosted SAP | **AWS Labs MCP + AgentCore Gateway** |
| Azure/Microsoft ecosystem | **Azure APIM with MCP + Entra ID** |
| Privacy-first, strict PII masking | **Lasso (Open Source + Commercial)** |
| Full custom control | **Lunar.dev Open Source** |
| Budget-constrained start | **Anthropic MCP Framework (Open Source)** |

---

## ✅ Must-Have Gateway Configuration Checklist

Regardless of which tool you choose, the implementation guide requires these to be proven complete [2]:

```
☐ Tool catalogue showing only 3 approved analyzers with "approved" status
☐ Successful schema validation test
☐ Rejected unauthorized-tool test (negative test)
☐ Gateway logs showing: Request ID | User | Tool | Result Status
☐ Tool versions recorded for audit comparability
☐ Failure behaviour defined: stop + safe explanation (never guess)
☐ Production write operations blocked and tested as blocked
☐ Secret rotation and expiry configured
☐ Environment separation: Dev / Test / Prod
```

---

## ⚠️ Key Guardrail Reminder

No matter which gateway technology you select, the implementation guide is clear [2]:

> *"ICA and Bob should not call raw tools directly"* — all calls **must** flow through the gateway, and if the gateway cannot validate a request, it **must stop** rather than pass it through.

---

**Bottom line:** For a pure SAP environment, **SAP Integration Suite's MCP Gateway** is the most architecturally aligned choice. For a hybrid or cloud-first setup, **AWS AgentCore** or **Azure APIM** with MCP support are strong commercial alternatives, while **Lunar.dev** or **Lasso** serve well as open-source foundations with strong security primitives.

| **Full request logging** | Log Request ID, user, tool, and result status |
| **Failure safety** | If validation fails → stop the request, never guess |
| **Tool versioning** | Record tool versions so reports can be compared over time |
| **Read-only enforcement** | Block any production write attempt automatically |

---

## 🌐 Open-Source MCP Gateway Options

### 1. 🥇 Lunar.dev Open Source MCP Gateway
- Sits between AI agents and MCP servers [1]
- Centralizes authentication, enforces access control, and logs every tool invocation
- Strong fit for the **allow-list + logging** requirements in this solution
- **Best for:** Teams wanting full control over their gateway infrastructure

### 2. AWS Labs MCP (Open Source)
- Available on GitHub (`awslabs/mcp`) [1]
- Includes direct resource management with security scanning and best practices
- Has an **AWS Systems Manager for SAP MCP Server** — directly relevant for SAP landscapes
- **Best for:** AWS-hosted SAP environments

### 3. MCP Protocol Native Framework (Anthropic)
- The Model Context Protocol itself is an **open standard and open-source framework** introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 [1]
- Provides the universal integration layer between AI systems and tools/data sources
- Acts as the foundational protocol on top of which any gateway can be built
- **Best for:** Building a custom, lightweight gateway from scratch

---

## 💼 Commercial MCP Gateway Options

### 4. SAP Integration Suite — MCP Gateway ⭐ *(Most Relevant)*
- SAP's own reference architecture explicitly supports **"MCP Gateway in SAP Integration Suite"** for exposing SAP and non-SAP APIs as a unified MCP tool catalog [1]
- Microsoft Copilot Studio agents authenticate to this gateway using **OAuth 2.0 Authorization** [1]
- **Best for:** SAP-centric environments — this is the most native fit for this solution

### 5. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
- Supports **OpenAPI targets (REST APIs)** with multiple authentication methods [1]
- Enterprise-grade managed service
- **Best for:** AWS-native deployments using Amazon Bedrock as the AI backbone

### 6. Azure API Management (APIM) with MCP Support
- Features **Azure AD/Entra ID native authentication** [1]
- Choice between open-source Kubernetes gateway and managed APIM option [1]
- **Best for:** Azure-centric enterprise environments with Microsoft identity infrastructure

### 7. Lasso Security-First MCP Gateway
- Features **PII masking with Presidio integration** — detects and redacts sensitive data automatically [1]
- Available as both Open-Source and Commercial deployment [1]
- **Best for:** Environments with strict data privacy requirements (aligns with the sensitive data masking guardrail) [2]

### 8. MuleSoft Omni Gateway (Flex Gateway)
- Envoy-based, ultrafast lightweight API gateway [1]
- Designed to manage and secure APIs running anywhere
- **Best for:** Organizations already using MuleSoft for SAP integration

---

## 🎯 Recommendation Matrix for This SAP Solution

| Scenario | Recommended Gateway |
|---|---|
| SAP-native, on-premise or BTP | **SAP Integration Suite MCP Gateway** |
| AWS-hosted SAP | **AWS Labs MCP + AgentCore Gateway** |
| Azure/Microsoft ecosystem | **Azure APIM with MCP + Entra ID** |
| Privacy-first, strict PII masking | **Lasso (Open Source + Commercial)** |
| Full custom control | **Lunar.dev Open Source** |
| Budget-constrained start | **Anthropic MCP Framework (Open Source)** |

---

## ✅ Must-Have Gateway Configuration Checklist

Regardless of which tool you choose, the implementation guide requires these to be proven complete [2]:

```
☐ Tool catalogue showing only 3 approved analyzers with "approved" status
☐ Successful schema validation test
☐ Rejected unauthorized-tool test (negative test)
☐ Gateway logs showing: Request ID | User | Tool | Result Status
☐ Tool versions recorded for audit comparability
☐ Failure behaviour defined: stop + safe explanation (never guess)
☐ Production write operations blocked and tested as blocked
☐ Secret rotation and expiry configured
☐ Environment separation: Dev / Test / Prod
```

---

## ⚠️ Key Guardrail Reminder

No matter which gateway technology you select, the implementation guide is clear [2]:

> *"ICA and Bob should not call raw tools directly"* — all calls **must** flow through the gateway, and if the gateway cannot validate a request, it **must stop** rather than pass it through.

---

**Bottom line:** For a pure SAP environment, **SAP Integration Suite's MCP Gateway** is the most architecturally aligned choice. For a hybrid or cloud-first setup, **AWS AgentCore** or **Azure APIM** with MCP support are strong commercial alternatives, while **Lunar.dev** or **Lasso** serve well as open-source foundations with strong security primitives.

# SAP Authorization Check Automation — Architecture & Data Flow

The diagram generation tool attempted to render the sequence diagram but returned a **400 Bad Request error** [1], meaning the visual could not be generated automatically. However, based on the full implementation guide, here is a complete and detailed textual architecture and data flow representation:

---

## 🏛️ High-Level Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SAP AUTHORIZATION CHECK AUTOMATION            │
│                     IBM Bob + ICA + MCP Gateway                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│    USER /    │────▶│       ICA        │────▶│    IBM BOB      │
│  REQUESTER   │◀────│  Conversational  │◀────│  Orchestrator   │
│              │     │   Assistant      │     │  (Governed)     │
└──────────────┘     └──────────────────┘     └────────┬────────┘
                                                        │
                                                        ▼
                                             ┌─────────────────────┐
                                             │    MCP GATEWAY      │
                                             │  ┌───────────────┐  │
                                             │  │ Authenticate  │  │
                                             │  │ Validate Token│  │
                                             │  │ Allow-List    │  │
                                             │  │ Rate Limit    │  │
                                             │  │ Log Calls     │  │
                                             │  └───────────────┘  │
                                             └──┬──────┬───────┬───┘
                                                │      │       │
                              ┌─────────────────┘      │       └──────────────────┐
                              ▼                         ▼                          ▼
                   ┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐
                   │  ABAP Analyzer   │    │  SU24 Analyzer   │    │  OData Analyzer      │
                   │                  │    │                  │    │                      │
                   │ AUTHORITY-CHECK  │    │ Proposal Compare │    │ Service Path Check   │
                   │ Line-level       │    │ Missing/Excess   │    │ Entity/Operation     │
                   │ Evidence +       │    │ Proposals +      │    │ DPC/DPC_EXT +        │
                   │ Confidence Score │    │ Corrections      │    │ Risk Classification  │
                   └────────┬─────────┘    └────────┬─────────┘    └──────────┬───────────┘
                            │                       │                          │
                            └───────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┘
                                                    ▼
                                         ┌─────────────────────┐
                                         │    AUDIT LOG        │
                                         │  Request ID | User  │
                                         │  Tool | Status      │
                                         └─────────────────────┘
```

---

## 🔄 Step-by-Step Data Flow

### Phase 1 — Conversational Intake (User ↔ ICA)

```
Step 1:  User submits ──────────────────────────────────────────▶ ICA
         • System & SAP release
         • Object / program / service name
         • Business action description
         • Change ticket reference

Step 2:  ICA asks clarifying questions ◀──────────────────────── ICA
         • Release confirmed?
         • Scope: ABAP / SU24 / OData / Combined?
         • Evidence type provided?

Step 3:  ICA shows confirmation screen ──────────────────────────▶ User
         "You are asking us to inspect X in system Y
          using evidence Z. Continue?"

Step 4:  User confirms ─────────────────────────────────────────▶ ICA
```

### Phase 2 — Sanitization & Routing (ICA → IBM Bob)

```
Step 5:  ICA applies data classification & privacy check
         • Removes passwords, tokens, personal identifiers
         • Assigns unique Request ID (e.g. AUTH-2026-00017)
         • Calculates input hash for traceability

Step 6:  ICA forwards sanitized intake package ─────────────────▶ IBM Bob
         Payload includes:
         {
           request_id: "AUTH-2026-00017",
           system: "S/4HANA Private Edition",
           scope: "ABAP_AUTHORITY_CHECK",
           evidence: [sanitized input],
           change_ticket: "CHG-XXXXX"
         }
```

### Phase 3 — Gateway Enforcement (IBM Bob → MCP Gateway)

```
Step 7:  IBM Bob routes tool call ──────────────────────────────▶ MCP Gateway
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Gateway checks:                      │
         │  ✅ Token valid?                     │
         │  ✅ Tool on allow-list?              │
         │  ✅ Schema valid?                    │
         │  ✅ Rate limit OK?                   │
         │  ❌ Unauthorized tool? → REJECT      │
         └─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Phase 4 — Analysis Execution (Gateway → 3 Analyzers)

```
Step 8a: Gateway invokes ───────────────────────────────────────▶ ABAP Analyzer
         Returns:
         • Exact code line with finding
         • Missing / weak / misplaced / unreachable check
         • Corrected pattern suggestion
         • Confidence score

Step 8b: Gateway invokes ───────────────────────────────────────▶ SU24 Analyzer
         Returns:
         • Missing or excessive proposals
         • Object + field comparison
         • Business impact explanation
         • Maintainable SU24 correction

Step 8c: Gateway invokes ───────────────────────────────────────▶ OData Analyzer
         Returns:
         • Service → Entity → Operation path
         • DPC/DPC_EXT authorization mapping
         • Gap between "technically reachable" vs "properly protected"
         • Risk classification
```

### Phase 5 — Report Compilation & Audit (Bob → ICA → User)

```
Step 9:  All findings return to IBM Bob via Gateway
         Bob compiles normalized finding record:
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ • Technical evidence (line/config)        │
         │ • Risk classification & severity          │
         │ • Confidence level & limitations          │
         │ • Correction guidance                     │
         │ • Normalized code/config sample           │
         │ • Remediation steps                       │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

Step 10: Bob logs to Audit Log ─────────────────────────────────▶ Audit Log
         Request ID | User | Tools Used | Result Status

Step 11: Gateway logs per tool ─────────────────────────────────▶ Audit Log
         tool=ABAP | status=complete
         tool=SU24 | status=complete
         tool=OData | status=complete

Step 12: ICA presents readable report ──────────────────────────▶ User
         + Human approval prompt
         "A qualified person must review and approve
          before any change is applied"
```

---

## 🛡️ Guardrails Embedded in the Flow

The following guardrails are enforced at each layer of the flow [2]:

| Layer | Guardrail Enforced |
|---|---|
| **ICA** | Sensitive data masking, confirmation before analysis, plain language output |
| **MCP Gateway** | Allow-list enforcement, token validation, rate limiting, full logging |
| **IBM Bob** | Scope control, only approved tools selected, stop if evidence insufficient |
| **Analyzers** | Read-only inspection, no execution of code, confidence + limitations shown |
| **Report** | Human approval mandatory, change must follow existing change management process |

---

## ⚠️ Critical Safety Rule

The entire flow is **diagnostic and read-only** for the first release [2]:

> *"It must not directly change SAP roles, SU24, ABAP code, OData configuration or production data. Any change must go through the existing human approval and change-management process."*

---
