## 🔄 Step-by-Step Data Flow

### Phase 1 — Conversational Intake (User ↔ ICA)

```
Step 1:  User submits ──────────────────────────────────────────▶ ICA
         • System & SAP release
         • Object / program / service name
         • Business action description
         • Change ticket reference

Step 2:  ICA asks clarifying questions ◀──────────────────────── ICA
         • Release confirmed?
         • Scope: ABAP / SU24 / OData / Combined?
         • Evidence type provided?

Step 3:  ICA shows confirmation screen ──────────────────────────▶ User
         "You are asking us to inspect X in system Y
          using evidence Z. Continue?"

Step 4:  User confirms ─────────────────────────────────────────▶ ICA
```

### Phase 2 — Sanitization & Routing (ICA → IBM Bob)

```
Step 5:  ICA applies data classification & privacy check
         • Removes passwords, tokens, personal identifiers
         • Assigns unique Request ID (e.g. AUTH-2026-00017)
         • Calculates input hash for traceability

Step 6:  ICA forwards sanitized intake package ─────────────────▶ IBM Bob
         Payload includes:
         {
           request_id: "AUTH-2026-00017",
           system: "S/4HANA Private Edition",
           scope: "ABAP_AUTHORITY_CHECK",
           evidence: [sanitized input],
           change_ticket: "CHG-XXXXX"
         }
```

### Phase 3 — Gateway Enforcement (IBM Bob → MCP Gateway)

```
Step 7:  IBM Bob routes tool call ──────────────────────────────▶ MCP Gateway
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ Gateway checks:                      │
         │  ✅ Token valid?                     │
         │  ✅ Tool on allow-list?              │
         │  ✅ Schema valid?                    │
         │  ✅ Rate limit OK?                   │
         │  ❌ Unauthorized tool? → REJECT      │
         └─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Phase 4 — Analysis Execution (Gateway → 3 Analyzers)

```
Step 8a: Gateway invokes ───────────────────────────────────────▶ ABAP Analyzer
         Returns:
         • Exact code line with finding
         • Missing / weak / misplaced / unreachable check
         • Corrected pattern suggestion
         • Confidence score

Step 8b: Gateway invokes ───────────────────────────────────────▶ SU24 Analyzer
         Returns:
         • Missing or excessive proposals
         • Object + field comparison
         • Business impact explanation
         • Maintainable SU24 correction

Step 8c: Gateway invokes ───────────────────────────────────────▶ OData Analyzer
         Returns:
         • Service → Entity → Operation path
         • DPC/DPC_EXT authorization mapping
         • Gap between "technically reachable" vs "properly protected"
         • Risk classification
```

### Phase 5 — Report Compilation & Audit (Bob → ICA → User)

```
Step 9:  All findings return to IBM Bob via Gateway
         Bob compiles normalized finding record:
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │ • Technical evidence (line/config)        │
         │ • Risk classification & severity          │
         │ • Confidence level & limitations          │
         │ • Correction guidance                     │
         │ • Normalized code/config sample           │
         │ • Remediation steps                       │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

Step 10: Bob logs to Audit Log ─────────────────────────────────▶ Audit Log
         Request ID | User | Tools Used | Result Status

Step 11: Gateway logs per tool ─────────────────────────────────▶ Audit Log
         tool=ABAP | status=complete
         tool=SU24 | status=complete
         tool=OData | status=complete

Step 12: ICA presents readable report ──────────────────────────▶ User
         + Human approval prompt
         "A qualified person must review and approve
          before any change is applied"
```

---

## 🛡️ Guardrails Embedded in the Flow

The following guardrails are enforced at each layer of the flow [2]:

| Layer | Guardrail Enforced |
|---|---|
| **ICA** | Sensitive data masking, confirmation before analysis, plain language output |
| **MCP Gateway** | Allow-list enforcement, token validation, rate limiting, full logging |
| **IBM Bob** | Scope control, only approved tools selected, stop if evidence insufficient |
| **Analyzers** | Read-only inspection, no execution of code, confidence + limitations shown |
| **Report** | Human approval mandatory, change must follow existing change management process |

---

The entire flow is **diagnostic and read-only** for the first release [2]:

> *"It must not directly change SAP roles, SU24, ABAP code, OData configuration or production data. Any change must go through the existing human approval and change-management process."*

# Sample ABAP Code: Correct vs. Missing AUTHORITY-CHECK

Based on the implementation guide, the ABAP analyzer reads approved source packages, looks for authorization-relevant statements, checks whether they are present in the right place, use the right objects and fields, and protect the sensitive business action — pointing to the **exact code line** that caused the finding [1].

Here are practical examples of what correct, missing, misplaced, and unreachable checks look like, and how the analyzer would flag each one.

---

## ✅ SCENARIO 1 — Correct AUTHORITY-CHECK (Pass)

This is what a **properly protected** sensitive business operation looks like:

```abap
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
* Program   : ZFI_CHANGE_DOCUMENT
* Action    : Change sales document for a specific company code
* Object    : F_BKPF_BUK (Accounting Document: Authorization for
*             Company Codes)
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
FORM change_document
  USING iv_bukrs TYPE bukrs
        iv_belnr TYPE belnr_d.

  " ✅ AUTHORITY-CHECK is placed BEFORE the sensitive operation
  " ✅ Correct authorization object: F_BKPF_BUK
  " ✅ Correct field: BUKRS (Company Code)
  " ✅ Correct activity: ACTVT '02' (Change)
  " ✅ Result is evaluated immediately after the check

  AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'
    ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    MESSAGE e001(zfi) WITH iv_bukrs.   " User not authorized
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  " --- Sensitive operation only proceeds if authorized ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🟢 Analyzer Finding — PASS
```
Finding ID  : AUTH-2026-00017-01
Checker     : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status      : PASS
Severity    : Informational
Line        : Line 18
Evidence    : AUTHORITY-CHECK on F_BKPF_BUK with BUKRS and ACTVT '02'
              placed before CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT' at line 26.
              Result evaluated at line 20 (sy-subrc <> 0).
Confidence  : HIGH — check is reachable, result is evaluated,
              fields match the declared business action.
Limitation  : Called routine 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT' not supplied;
              internal checks within it were not verified.
```

---

## ❌ SCENARIO 2 — Missing AUTHORITY-CHECK (Test Case T02)

The sensitive operation proceeds with **no check at all** [1]:

```abap
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
* Program   : ZFI_CHANGE_DOCUMENT
* Action    : Change sales document for a specific company code
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
FORM change_document
  USING iv_bukrs TYPE bukrs
        iv_belnr TYPE belnr_d.

  " ❌ NO AUTHORITY-CHECK anywhere before the sensitive operation
  " ❌ Any user who can reach this form can change any document
  " ❌ Company code (BUKRS) is never validated against user authorization

  " --- Sensitive operation runs WITHOUT any authorization gate ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'        " <-- LINE 13: UNPROTECTED
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🔴 Analyzer Finding — CRITICAL
```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-00017-02
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH — any authenticated user can change documents
               for any company code
Line         : Line 13 — CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'
Evidence     : No AUTHORITY-CHECK statement found in FORM
               change_document or its directly visible call path
               before the sensitive operation at line 13.
Risk         : A user without company-code authorization can
               change accounting documents, bypassing financial
               controls.
Confidence   : HIGH — the check is absent from the supplied source.
               Lower confidence if the check exists in a called
               routine not included in the input package.
Limitation   : Called routines not supplied in the input package
               were not verified.

Recommended Correction:
  Add AUTHORITY-CHECK on object F_BKPF_BUK before line 13.
  Evaluate sy-subrc immediately and exit if not authorized.

  AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'
    ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.
  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    MESSAGE e001(zfi) WITH iv_bukrs.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

Retest Plan  : T-positive — authorized user changes document → allowed.
               T-negative — unauthorized user attempts → rejected with
               message.
```

---

## ⚠️ SCENARIO 3 — Check Exists but Result is Never Evaluated (Weak Check)

A common and dangerous pattern — the check is present but **ignored** [1]:

```abap
FORM change_document
  USING iv_bukrs TYPE bukrs
        iv_belnr TYPE belnr_d.

  " ⚠️ AUTHORITY-CHECK exists — but sy-subrc is NEVER evaluated
  " ⚠️ The operation proceeds regardless of authorization result
  " ⚠️ This gives a FALSE sense of security

  AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'   " <-- LINE 8
    ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

  " ❌ Missing: IF sy-subrc <> 0 check here

  " --- Sensitive operation runs even if check FAILED ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'        " <-- LINE 15: UNPROTECTED
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🟠 Analyzer Finding — HIGH
```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-00017-03
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH — authorization check result is never evaluated
Line         : Line 8 — AUTHORITY-CHECK present
               Line 15 — CALL FUNCTION proceeds regardless
Evidence     : AUTHORITY-CHECK found at line 8. No evaluation of
               sy-subrc between line 8 and the sensitive operation
               at line 15. The check has no enforcement effect.
Risk         : Equivalent to no check — unauthorized users can
               proceed to the sensitive operation.
Confidence   : HIGH
Recommended  : Add sy-subrc evaluation immediately after line 8
Correction   :
  AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'
    ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.
  IF sy-subrc <> 0.          " <-- ADD THIS
    MESSAGE e001(zfi) WITH iv_bukrs.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.
```

---

## 🔀 SCENARIO 4 — Check in Unreachable Branch (Test Case T03)

The check exists but is **only reached under a condition that never triggers** in the sensitive path [1]:

```abap
FORM change_document
  USING iv_bukrs TYPE bukrs
        iv_belnr TYPE belnr_d
        iv_mode  TYPE char1.   " Passed as 'C' (Change) always

  " ❌ Authority check only runs in the 'D' (Display) branch
  " ❌ The 'C' (Change) path — the sensitive one — is unprotected

  IF iv_mode = 'D'.                        " <-- This branch = Display
    AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'   " <-- LINE 9: only for Display
      ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
      ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '03'.              " ACTVT 03 = Display only
    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  " --- Change operation runs with NO check for ACTVT '02' ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'          " <-- LINE 18: UNPROTECTED
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🟠 Analyzer Finding — HIGH
```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-00017-04
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH
Line         : Line 9 — AUTHORITY-CHECK reachable only when
               iv_mode = 'D' (Display)
               Line 18 — CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT' reachable
               when iv_mode = 'C' (Change) — NOT protected
Evidence     : AUTHORITY-CHECK at line 9 checks ACTVT '03' (Display)
               only within the iv_mode = 'D' branch.
               The sensitive Change operation at line 18 is outside
               this branch and has no corresponding ACTVT '02' check.
Risk         : The change path is entirely unprotected. Any user
               reaching this form with iv_mode = 'C' can change
               documents for any company code.
Confidence   : MEDIUM-HIGH — reachability depends on how iv_mode is
               populated by the caller; caller code not supplied.
Limitation   : Calling program not included in the input package.
               Confidence would increase if caller evidence confirms
               iv_mode is always 'C' for the change path.
Recommended  : Add a separate AUTHORITY-CHECK for ACTVT '02' before
Correction     line 18, outside the iv_mode = 'D' condition block.
```

---

## 📋 Summary: How the Analyzer Evaluates Each Pattern

The analyzer checks four questions for every sensitive operation [1]:

| Question | Scenario 1 ✅ | Scenario 2 ❌ | Scenario 3 ⚠️ | Scenario 4 🔀 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Does the check exist?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ✅ Partially |
| **Is it reachable in the code path?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ N/A | ✅ Yes | ❌ Not for Change |
| **Is the result actually evaluated?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ N/A | ❌ No | ✅ Yes (for Display only) |
| **Do the fields match the business action?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ N/A | ⚠️ Moot | ❌ Wrong ACTVT |

---

## 🛡️ Key Analyzer Safety Rules Applied

All of the above findings follow the core rules from the implementation guide [1]:

- The source code is treated as **text to inspect, not code to execute** [1]
- Every finding points to the **exact line number** causing the issue [1]
- **Confidence level and limitations** are always shown — especially when called routines were not supplied in the input package [1]
- The corrected example is clearly labelled as a **recommendation requiring developer and SAP Security review** — it is never applied automatically [1]
- The solution **must say "not enough evidence"** and request more information rather than guess [1]

Would you like to see equivalent examples for the **SU24 Analyzer** or the **OData Authorization Analyzer**?

    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    MESSAGE e001(zfi) WITH iv_bukrs.   " User not authorized
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  " --- Sensitive operation only proceeds if authorized ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🟢 Analyzer Finding — PASS
```
Finding ID  : AUTH-2026-00017-01
Checker     : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status      : PASS
Severity    : Informational
Line        : Line 18
Evidence    : AUTHORITY-CHECK on F_BKPF_BUK with BUKRS and ACTVT '02'
              placed before CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT' at line 26.
              Result evaluated at line 20 (sy-subrc <> 0).
Confidence  : HIGH — check is reachable, result is evaluated,
              fields match the declared business action.
Limitation  : Called routine 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT' not supplied;
              internal checks within it were not verified.
```

---

## ❌ SCENARIO 2 — Missing AUTHORITY-CHECK (Test Case T02)

The sensitive operation proceeds with **no check at all** [1]:

```abap
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
* Program   : ZFI_CHANGE_DOCUMENT
* Action    : Change sales document for a specific company code
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
FORM change_document
  USING iv_bukrs TYPE bukrs
        iv_belnr TYPE belnr_d.

  " ❌ NO AUTHORITY-CHECK anywhere before the sensitive operation
  " ❌ Any user who can reach this form can change any document
  " ❌ Company code (BUKRS) is never validated against user authorization

  " --- Sensitive operation runs WITHOUT any authorization gate ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'        " <-- LINE 13: UNPROTECTED
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🔴 Analyzer Finding — CRITICAL
```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-00017-02
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH — any authenticated user can change documents
               for any company code
Line         : Line 13 — CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'
Evidence     : No AUTHORITY-CHECK statement found in FORM
               change_document or its directly visible call path
               before the sensitive operation at line 13.
Risk         : A user without company-code authorization can
               change accounting documents, bypassing financial
               controls.
Confidence   : HIGH — the check is absent from the supplied source.
               Lower confidence if the check exists in a called
               routine not included in the input package.
Limitation   : Called routines not supplied in the input package
               were not verified.

Recommended Correction:
  Add AUTHORITY-CHECK on object F_BKPF_BUK before line 13.
  Evaluate sy-subrc immediately and exit if not authorized.

  AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'
    ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.
  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    MESSAGE e001(zfi) WITH iv_bukrs.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

Retest Plan  : T-positive — authorized user changes document → allowed.
               T-negative — unauthorized user attempts → rejected with
               message.
```

---

## ⚠️ SCENARIO 3 — Check Exists but Result is Never Evaluated (Weak Check)

A common and dangerous pattern — the check is present but **ignored** [1]:

```abap
FORM change_document
  USING iv_bukrs TYPE bukrs
        iv_belnr TYPE belnr_d.

  " ⚠️ AUTHORITY-CHECK exists — but sy-subrc is NEVER evaluated
  " ⚠️ The operation proceeds regardless of authorization result
  " ⚠️ This gives a FALSE sense of security

  AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'   " <-- LINE 8
    ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

  " ❌ Missing: IF sy-subrc <> 0 check here

  " --- Sensitive operation runs even if check FAILED ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'        " <-- LINE 15: UNPROTECTED
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🟠 Analyzer Finding — HIGH
```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-00017-03
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH — authorization check result is never evaluated
Line         : Line 8 — AUTHORITY-CHECK present
               Line 15 — CALL FUNCTION proceeds regardless
Evidence     : AUTHORITY-CHECK found at line 8. No evaluation of
               sy-subrc between line 8 and the sensitive operation
               at line 15. The check has no enforcement effect.
Risk         : Equivalent to no check — unauthorized users can
               proceed to the sensitive operation.
Confidence   : HIGH
Recommended  : Add sy-subrc evaluation immediately after line 8
Correction   :
  AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'
    ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
    ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.
  IF sy-subrc <> 0.          " <-- ADD THIS
    MESSAGE e001(zfi) WITH iv_bukrs.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.
```

---

## 🔀 SCENARIO 4 — Check in Unreachable Branch (Test Case T03)

The check exists but is **only reached under a condition that never triggers** in the sensitive path [1]:

```abap
FORM change_document
  USING iv_bukrs TYPE bukrs
        iv_belnr TYPE belnr_d
        iv_mode  TYPE char1.   " Passed as 'C' (Change) always

  " ❌ Authority check only runs in the 'D' (Display) branch
  " ❌ The 'C' (Change) path — the sensitive one — is unprotected

  IF iv_mode = 'D'.                        " <-- This branch = Display
    AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'F_BKPF_BUK'   " <-- LINE 9: only for Display
      ID 'BUKRS' FIELD iv_bukrs
      ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '03'.              " ACTVT 03 = Display only
    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  " --- Change operation runs with NO check for ACTVT '02' ---
  CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'          " <-- LINE 18: UNPROTECTED
    EXPORTING
      i_bukrs = iv_bukrs
      i_belnr = iv_belnr.

ENDFORM.
```

### 🟠 Analyzer Finding — HIGH
```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-00017-04
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH
Line         : Line 9 — AUTHORITY-CHECK reachable only when
               iv_mode = 'D' (Display)
               Line 18 — CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT' reachable
               when iv_mode = 'C' (Change) — NOT protected
Evidence     : AUTHORITY-CHECK at line 9 checks ACTVT '03' (Display)
               only within the iv_mode = 'D' branch.
               The sensitive Change operation at line 18 is outside
               this branch and has no corresponding ACTVT '02' check.
Risk         : The change path is entirely unprotected. Any user
               reaching this form with iv_mode = 'C' can change
               documents for any company code.
Confidence   : MEDIUM-HIGH — reachability depends on how iv_mode is
               populated by the caller; caller code not supplied.
Limitation   : Calling program not included in the input package.
               Confidence would increase if caller evidence confirms
               iv_mode is always 'C' for the change path.
Recommended  : Add a separate AUTHORITY-CHECK for ACTVT '02' before
Correction     line 18, outside the iv_mode = 'D' condition block.
```

---

## 📋 Summary: How the Analyzer Evaluates Each Pattern

The analyzer checks four questions for every sensitive operation [1]:

| Question | Scenario 1 ✅ | Scenario 2 ❌ | Scenario 3 ⚠️ | Scenario 4 🔀 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Does the check exist?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ✅ Partially |
| **Is it reachable in the code path?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ N/A | ✅ Yes | ❌ Not for Change |
| **Is the result actually evaluated?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ N/A | ❌ No | ✅ Yes (for Display only) |
| **Do the fields match the business action?** | ✅ Yes | ❌ N/A | ⚠️ Moot | ❌ Wrong ACTVT |

---

## 🛡️ Key Analyzer Safety Rules Applied

All of the above findings follow the core rules from the implementation guide [1]:

- The source code is treated as **text to inspect, not code to execute** [1]
- Every finding points to the **exact line number** causing the issue [1]
- **Confidence level and limitations** are always shown — especially when called routines were not supplied in the input package [1]
- The corrected example is clearly labelled as a **recommendation requiring developer and SAP Security review** — it is never applied automatically [1]
- The solution **must say "not enough evidence"** and request more information rather than guess [1]

## 3.2 SU24 analyzer
SU24 is used to maintain authorization proposals for transactions and applications. In simple terms, it helps SAP know which authorization objects should normally be considered when a transaction is used. The analyzer compares the requested business action with the proposal information and identifies missing, weak, excessive or inconsistent entries.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDE
IBM BOB + ICA

# SAP Authorization Check Automation

SU24 analyzer Checks whether transaction defaults support the intended authorization design. Finds missing or excessive proposals and suggests maintainable corrections. OData analyzer Checks service entry points and how business operations are protected. Finds missing or weak authorization controls around the service.

- Points to mail statement and code line
- Suggests corrected patterns
- Confidence and evidence
B. SU24 ANALYZER
- Compares transaction and authorization default proposals
- Detects missing or excessive proposals
- Explains impact
- Recommends maintainable SU24 correction
C. ODATA AUTHORIZATION ANALYZER
- Checks service activation, entity set, operation, DPC/DPC_EXT or behavior implementation, authorization mapping and gateway exposure
- Identifies missing checks
- Recommends correction

### What to do
 Read the approved SU24 export or equivalent evidence using a read-only connection or sanitized file.
 Identify the transaction, application, authorization object, field and proposal status.
 Compare the expected business action with the available proposal information.
 Detect missing proposals, proposals that are too broad, proposals that do not match the operation, and evidence that is too old or incomplete.

### What proves that the step is complete
 Unit tests for present, missing, misplaced and unreachable checks.
 Line-level evidence test.
 Called-routine limitation test.
 False-positive review by an ABAP and SAP Security expert.
Primary owner: ABAP engineering owner with SAP Security

## Step 8: Implement the SU24 analyzer
In simple words: This component checks whether the authorization proposals support the intended transaction or application design.

T03 ABAP check exists only in unreachable branch Finding explains reachability concern and confidence. T04 SU24 proposal is missing Finding identifies transaction/object/field and safe proposal correction. T05 SU24 proposal is too broad Warning separates proposal issue from role-design issue.

# 3. The three security analyzers  
## 3.1 ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK analyzer
This analyzer reads an approved ABAP source package. It looks for authorization-relevant statements and checks whether they are present in the right place, use the right object and fields, and protect the sensitive business action. It should point to the exact code line or statement that caused the finding.
 Example question: "Does this program check whether the user may change the company code before saving the document?"

For SU24, capture transaction or application name, intended business action, expected authorization objects and existing proposal evidence.
 For OData, capture service name, version, entity set, operation, application or tile, implementation reference and test evidence.
 Add a privacy step that removes passwords, tokens, personal identifiers, customer data and unrelated production content.

### What proves that the step is complete
 Positive and negative SU24 samples.
 Object and field comparison test.
 Broad-access warning test.
 Recommendation reviewed by SAP Security and Basis or development owner.
Primary owner: SAP Security / GRC owner

## Step 9: Implement the OData authorization analyzer
In simple words: This component follows the service path and checks whether the exposed business operation is properly protected.

ABAP / SAP Development Code correction, implementation evidence and developer retest. Final security approval. Fiori / Gateway specialist Service metadata and OData implementation evidence. Business role approval. AI Platform / MCP Gateway, Bob/ICA integration, tool catalogue, SAP policy decisions. owner reliability and logging.

## 3.3 OData authorization analyzer
OData services are used by many SAP Fiori applications and integrations. This analyzer follows the service path: service, entity, operation, implementation and authorization decision. It looks for a gap between "the service is technically reachable" and "the business action is properly protected."
 Example question: "Can this Fiori service read or change data without checking the user's company code or business role?"

- Collects missing details
MCP Gateway - approved tool directory
- Authenticates request
- Validates token
- Enforces allow list and rate limits
- Logs calls
IBM Bob - governed orchestration
- Selects only approved tools
- Knows the approved three-checker scope
- Sends normalized input
- Receives structured results  
3. THREE ANALYSIS ENGINES
A. ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK ANALYZER
- Finds missing, weak, misplaced or unpatchable AUTHORITY-CHECK statements
- Points to mail statement and code line

## Step 7: Implement the ABAP analyzer

# SAP Authorization Check Analysis — ME22N Purchase Order Change

## 🔍 Intake Confirmation

Before I proceed, here is a summary of your request:

> **You are asking me to inspect:** An ABAP program calling `CHANGE_DOCUMENT` without an `AUTHORITY-CHECK` before it
> **System:** S/4HANA
> **Transaction:** ME22N (Change Purchase Order)
> **Concern:** Missing authorization check before a sensitive change operation

**Confirm to continue? → Yes / No**

---

## 🔴 Finding — Missing AUTHORITY-CHECK Before Sensitive Operation

Based on your description, this matches exactly the pattern the ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer is designed to detect [1]. The analyzer reads an approved ABAP source package, looks for authorization-relevant statements, and checks whether they are present in the right place, use the right object and fields, and protect the sensitive business action — pointing to the exact code line or statement that caused the finding [1].

---

## 📋 Finding Record

```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-ME22N-01
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Transaction  : ME22N — Change Purchase Order
System       : S/4HANA
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH
```

---

## ⚠️ What Was Found

The program performs a sensitive **change operation** for a purchase order via `CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'`, but the supplied description confirms **no AUTHORITY-CHECK statement exists** before this call [1].

> *"The program performs a sensitive change for a document, but the supplied code does not show an authorization check immediately before the change. The analyzer points to the exact statement. The likely risk is that a user who can reach the program may perform the action outside the intended business-role boundary."* [1]

---

## 🏢 Business Impact

For **ME22N — Change Purchase Order**, the following authorization objects are typically required for proper protection:

| Authorization Object | Field | Required Activity | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `M_BEST_BSA` | `BSART` | `02` (Change) | Purchase order document type |
| `M_BEST_EKO` | `EKORG` | `02` (Change) | Purchasing organization restriction |
| `M_BEST_EKG` | `EKGRP` | `02` (Change) | Purchasing group restriction |
| `M_BEST_WRK` | `WERKS` | `02` (Change) | Plant restriction |

Without these checks, **any user who can reach this program can change purchase orders across all purchasing organizations, groups, and plants** — bypassing critical procurement controls.

---

## ✅ Recommended Correction Pattern

Add the following `AUTHORITY-CHECK` block **immediately before** the `CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'` statement:

```abap
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
* Authorization check BEFORE purchase order change
* Transaction : ME22N
* Object      : M_BEST_EKO — Purchasing Organization
*----------------------------------------------------------------------

" Step 1: Check Purchasing Organization authorization
AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'M_BEST_EKO'
  ID 'EKORG' FIELD lv_ekorg
  ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.          " '02' = Change

IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  MESSAGE e001(zmm)
    WITH 'Not authorized to change PO for purchasing org' lv_ekorg.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

" Step 2: Check Purchasing Group authorization
AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'M_BEST_EKG'
  ID 'EKGRP' FIELD lv_ekgrp
  ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  MESSAGE e002(zmm)
    WITH 'Not authorized for purchasing group' lv_ekgrp.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

" Step 3: Check Document Type authorization
AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'M_BEST_BSA'
  ID 'BSART' FIELD lv_bsart
  ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  MESSAGE e003(zmm)
    WITH 'Not authorized for document type' lv_bsart.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

" --- Only now proceed with the change operation ---
CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'
  EXPORTING
    ...
```

---

## 📊 Confidence & Limitations

```
Confidence   : HIGH — based on your description, no AUTHORITY-CHECK
               exists before the CHANGE_DOCUMENT call.

Limitation   : Confidence would be MEDIUM if the authorization
               decision exists inside a called routine that was
               not included in the input package [1].
               Please supply the full source including all called
               routines for a complete review.
```

As the implementation guide states [1]:

> *"The result must be rechecked if the authorization decision happens in a called routine that was not included."*

---

## 🔄 Recommended Next Steps

Following the approved remediation workflow [1]:

| Step | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Review** | SAP Security confirms correct objects and field values for ME22N | SAP Security |
| **2. Correct** | Developer adds the approved authorization-check pattern | ABAP Developer |
| **3. Transport** | Change is transported through the normal change process | Change Management |
| **4. Retest** | Positive test (authorized user changes PO → allowed) + Negative test (unauthorized user → rejected with message) | Developer + SAP Security |

---

## ⚠️ Important Safety Boundary

This analysis is **diagnostic and read-only** [1]:

> *"The first release must be diagnostic and read-only. It must not directly change SAP roles, SU24, ABAP code, OData configuration or production data. Any change must go through the existing human approval and change-management process."* [1]

# SAP Authorization Check Analysis — ME22N Purchase Order Change

## 🔍 Intake Confirmation

Before I proceed, here is a summary of your request:

> **You are asking me to inspect:** An ABAP program calling `CHANGE_DOCUMENT` without an `AUTHORITY-CHECK` before it
> **System:** S/4HANA
> **Transaction:** ME22N (Change Purchase Order)
> **Concern:** Missing authorization check before a sensitive change operation

**Confirm to continue? → Yes / No**

---

## 🔴 Finding — Missing AUTHORITY-CHECK Before Sensitive Operation

Based on your description, this matches exactly the pattern the ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer is designed to detect [1]. The analyzer reads an approved ABAP source package, looks for authorization-relevant statements, and checks whether they are present in the right place, use the right object and fields, and protect the sensitive business action — pointing to the exact code line or statement that caused the finding [1].

---

## 📋 Finding Record

```
Finding ID   : AUTH-2026-ME22N-01
Checker      : ABAP AUTHORITY-CHECK Analyzer
Transaction  : ME22N — Change Purchase Order
System       : S/4HANA
Status       : FINDING
Severity     : HIGH
```

---

## ⚠️ What Was Found

The program performs a sensitive **change operation** for a purchase order via `CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'`, but the supplied description confirms **no AUTHORITY-CHECK statement exists** before this call [1].

> *"The program performs a sensitive change for a document, but the supplied code does not show an authorization check immediately before the change. The analyzer points to the exact statement. The likely risk is that a user who can reach the program may perform the action outside the intended business-role boundary."* [1]

---

## 🏢 Business Impact

For **ME22N — Change Purchase Order**, the following authorization objects are typically required for proper protection:

| Authorization Object | Field | Required Activity | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `M_BEST_BSA` | `BSART` | `02` (Change) | Purchase order document type |
| `M_BEST_EKO` | `EKORG` | `02` (Change) | Purchasing organization restriction |
| `M_BEST_EKG` | `EKGRP` | `02` (Change) | Purchasing group restriction |
| `M_BEST_WRK` | `WERKS` | `02` (Change) | Plant restriction |

Without these checks, **any user who can reach this program can change purchase orders across all purchasing organizations, groups, and plants** — bypassing critical procurement controls.

---

## ✅ Recommended Correction Pattern

Add the following `AUTHORITY-CHECK` block **immediately before** the `CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'` statement:

```abap
*----------------------------------------------------------------------
* Authorization check BEFORE purchase order change
* Transaction : ME22N
* Object      : M_BEST_EKO — Purchasing Organization
*----------------------------------------------------------------------

" Step 1: Check Purchasing Organization authorization
AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'M_BEST_EKO'
  ID 'EKORG' FIELD lv_ekorg
  ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.          " '02' = Change

IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  MESSAGE e001(zmm)
    WITH 'Not authorized to change PO for purchasing org' lv_ekorg.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

" Step 2: Check Purchasing Group authorization
AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'M_BEST_EKG'
  ID 'EKGRP' FIELD lv_ekgrp
  ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  MESSAGE e002(zmm)
    WITH 'Not authorized for purchasing group' lv_ekgrp.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

" Step 3: Check Document Type authorization
AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'M_BEST_BSA'
  ID 'BSART' FIELD lv_bsart
  ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '02'.

IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  MESSAGE e003(zmm)
    WITH 'Not authorized for document type' lv_bsart.
  RETURN.
ENDIF.

" --- Only now proceed with the change operation ---
CALL FUNCTION 'CHANGE_DOCUMENT'
  EXPORTING
    ...
```

---

## 📊 Confidence & Limitations

```
Confidence   : HIGH — based on your description, no AUTHORITY-CHECK
               exists before the CHANGE_DOCUMENT call.

Limitation   : Confidence would be MEDIUM if the authorization
               decision exists inside a called routine that was
               not included in the input package [1].
               Please supply the full source including all called
               routines for a complete review.
```

As the implementation guide states [1]:

> *"The result must be rechecked if the authorization decision happens in a called routine that was not included."*

---

## 🔄 Recommended Next Steps

Following the approved remediation workflow [1]:

| Step | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Review** | SAP Security confirms correct objects and field values for ME22N | SAP Security |
| **2. Correct** | Developer adds the approved authorization-check pattern | ABAP Developer |
| **3. Transport** | Change is transported through the normal change process | Change Management |
| **4. Retest** | Positive test (authorized user changes PO → allowed) + Negative test (unauthorized user → rejected with message) | Developer + SAP Security |

---

## ⚠️ Important Safety Boundary

This analysis is **diagnostic and read-only** [1]:

> *"The first release must be diagnostic and read-only. It must not directly change SAP roles, SU24, ABAP code, OData configuration or production data. Any change must go through the existing human approval and change-management process."* [1]

# SU24 Proposal Check for ME22N — Yes, Absolutely

Yes, I strongly recommend checking the SU24 proposal for ME22N. This is a critical complementary step to your ABAP authorization check [1].

---

## Why This Matters

The SU24 analyzer checks whether transaction defaults support the intended authorization design [1]. For ME22N, the SU24 proposal determines which authorization objects will be included when roles are generated using the Profile Generator [1].

Here's the dependency chain:

1. **Your ABAP code** has the `AUTHORITY-CHECK` statements (which you just corrected)
2. **SU24 proposal** must list the objects being checked (M_BEST_EKO, M_BEST_EKG, M_BEST_BSA)
3. **Role generation** includes those objects only if SU24 proposes them
4. **User gets access** only if the role contains the correct fields with the right values

If the SU24 proposal is missing or too broad, roles generated for ME22N will be incomplete or overly permissive — **even if your ABAP code checks correctly** [1].

---

## What the SU24 Analyzer Will Check

The analyzer will [1]:

- Read the approved SU24 export or equivalent evidence using a read-only connection
- Identify the transaction (ME22N), authorization objects, fields, and proposal status
- Compare the expected business action (Change PO) with the available proposal information
- Detect missing proposals, proposals that are too broad, proposals that do not match the operation, and evidence that is too old or incomplete

---

## What to Provide for the SU24 Check

To proceed, I need [1]:

| Information | Example |
|---|---|
| **Transaction name** | ME22N |
| **Intended business action** | Change purchase order with organizational restrictions |
| **Expected authorization objects** | M_BEST_EKO, M_BEST_EKG, M_BEST_BSA |
| **Existing proposal evidence** | Current SU24 export or transaction maintenance screenshot |
| **System & Release** | S/4HANA (which release?) |
| **Change ticket** | Reference number for tracking |

---

## Recommended Next Question

**Please provide:**

> *"Can you show me the current SU24 proposal for ME22N? I need to see which authorization objects are listed and whether M_BEST_EKO, M_BEST_EKG, and M_BEST_BSA are marked as 'Check' or 'No Check' for each field."*

Once you provide that, the SU24 analyzer will identify:
- ✅ If all three objects are present with the right "Check" status
- ❌ If any are missing (finding: T04 — SU24 proposal is missing)
- ⚠️ If any are set to "No Check" when they should be "Check" (finding: T05 — SU24 proposal is too broad)

Would you like to provide the SU24 proposal evidence now, or do you need guidance on how to extract it from your SAP system?

3. **Role generation** includes those objects only if SU24 proposes them
4. **User gets access** only if the role contains the correct fields with the right values

If the SU24 proposal is missing or too broad, roles generated for ME22N will be incomplete or overly permissive — **even if your ABAP code checks correctly** [1].

---

## What the SU24 Analyzer Will Check

The analyzer will [1]:

- Read the approved SU24 export or equivalent evidence using a read-only connection
- Identify the transaction (ME22N), authorization objects, fields, and proposal status
- Compare the expected business action (Change PO) with the available proposal information
- Detect missing proposals, proposals that are too broad, proposals that do not match the operation, and evidence that is too old or incomplete

---

## What to Provide for the SU24 Check

To proceed, I need [1]:

| Information | Example |
|---|---|
| **Transaction name** | ME22N |
| **Intended business action** | Change purchase order with organizational restrictions |
| **Expected authorization objects** | M_BEST_EKO, M_BEST_EKG, M_BEST_BSA |
| **Existing proposal evidence** | Current SU24 export or transaction maintenance screenshot |
| **System & Release** | S/4HANA (which release?) |

Once you provide that, the SU24 analyzer will identify:
- ✅ If all three objects are present with the right "Check" status
- ❌ If any are missing (finding: T04 — SU24 proposal is missing)
- ⚠️ If any are set to "No Check" when they should be "Check" (finding: T05 — SU24 proposal is too broad)

messages.content: Can you help me deploy the UTSAV_Authority-Check chatbot to SAP BTP or our corporate cloud environment?

# Deploying UTSAV_Authority-Check to SAP BTP or Corporate Cloud

Based on the implementation guide, the chatbot must be deployed following the governed architecture with read-only boundaries, full audit trail, and human approval workflows maintained throughout [1]. Here is a complete deployment guide for both options.

---

## 🏗️ Option A — SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) Deployment

### Step 1: Prerequisites & Account Setup

```
SAP BTP Requirements:
☐ SAP BTP Global Account with subaccount
☐ Cloud Foundry environment enabled
☐ SAP Build Work Zone (optional — for portal embedding)
☐ SAP Authorization & Trust Management Service (XSUAA)
☐ BTP Connectivity Service (for SAP backend connections)
☐ Destination Service configured
```

### Step 2: Prepare the Application Structure

Create the following folder structure on your local machine:

```
UTSAV_Authority-Check/
│
├── manifest.yml              ← Cloud Foundry deployment config
├── package.json              ← Node.js app descriptor
├── server.js                 ← Express web server
├── xs-security.json          ← XSUAA security config
├── xs-app.json               ← App Router config
│
└── app/
    └── UTSAV_Authority-Check.html   ← Your chatbot HTML file
```

### Step 3: Create the Server Files

**`server.js`** — Simple Express server to serve your HTML:

```javascript
// server.js
// UTSAV_Authority-Check — SAP BTP Express Server
// Read-only diagnostic tool — Implementation Guide [1]

const express = require('express');
const path    = require('path');
const app     = express();
const PORT    = process.env.PORT || 8080;

// Serve static files from /app folder
app.use(express.static(path.join(__dirname, 'app')));

// Security headers — enforce read-only boundary [1]
app.use((req, res, next) => {
    res.setHeader('X-Content-Type-Options',    'nosniff');
    res.setHeader('X-Frame-Options',           'SAMEORIGIN');
    res.setHeader('X-XSS-Protection',          '1; mode=block');
    res.setHeader('Strict-Transport-Security', 'max-age=31536000');
    res.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy',
        "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'");
    next();
});

// Root route — serve the chatbot
app.get('/', (req, res) => {
    res.sendFile(path.join(__dirname, 'app', 'UTSAV_Authority-Check.html'));
});

// Health check endpoint
app.get('/health', (req, res) => {
    res.json({
        status:    'healthy',
        app:       'UTSAV_Authority-Check',
        version:   '1.0.0',
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        boundary:  'read-only-diagnostic'
    });
});

app.listen(PORT, () => {
    console.log(`UTSAV_Authority-Check running on port ${PORT}`);
});
```

**`package.json`** — Node.js descriptor:

```json
{
  "name": "utsav-authority-check",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "SAP Authorization Check Assistant — IBM Bob + ICA",
  "main": "server.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node server.js"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.2"
  },
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=18.0.0"
  }
}
```

**`manifest.yml`** — Cloud Foundry deployment config:

```yaml
---
applications:
  - name: utsav-authority-check
    memory: 256M
    disk_quota: 512M
    instances: 1
    buildpacks:
      - nodejs_buildpack
    command: node server.js
    routes:
      - route: utsav-authority-check.<your-btp-subdomain>.cfapps.<region>.hana.ondemand.com
    env:
      NODE_ENV: production
      APP_NAME: UTSAV_Authority-Check
      BOUNDARY: read-only-diagnostic
    services:
      - utsav-xsuaa
```

**`xs-security.json`** — XSUAA security descriptor:

```json
{
  "xsappname": "utsav-authority-check",
  "tenant-mode": "dedicated",
  "description": "UTSAV Authority Check — SAP Authorization Assistant",
  "scopes": [
    {
      "name": "$XSAPPNAME.Viewer",
      "description": "View and use the authorization check assistant"
    },
    {
      "name": "$XSAPPNAME.SecurityReviewer",
      "description": "SAP Security team — approve findings"
    }
  ],
  "role-templates": [
    {
      "name": "Viewer",
      "description": "Can use the UTSAV Authority Check assistant",
      "scope-references": ["$XSAPPNAME.Viewer"]
    },
    {
      "name": "SecurityReviewer",
      "description": "SAP Security team member — can approve findings",
      "scope-references": [
        "$XSAPPNAME.Viewer",
        "$XSAPPNAME.SecurityReviewer"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**`xs-app.json`** — App Router configuration:

```json
{
  "welcomeFile": "/UTSAV_Authority-Check.html",
  "authenticationMethod": "route",
  "routes": [
    {
      "source": "^/(.*)$",
      "target": "$1",
      "localDir": "app",
      "authenticationType": "xsuaa"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Step 4: Deploy to SAP BTP — Command by Command

Open your terminal and run these commands in order:

```bash
# Step 4.1 — Login to SAP BTP Cloud Foundry
cf login -a https://api.cf.<your-region>.hana.ondemand.com \
         -u <your-email> \
         -p <your-password> \
         -o <your-org> \
         -s <your-space>

# Step 4.2 — Create XSUAA service instance
cf create-service xsuaa application utsav-xsuaa \
  -c xs-security.json

# Step 4.3 — Install Node dependencies
npm install

# Step 4.4 — Deploy the application
cf push utsav-authority-check -f manifest.yml

# Step 4.5 — Verify deployment
cf apps
cf logs utsav-authority-check --recent

# Step 4.6 — Get your public URL
cf app utsav-authority-check
```

### Step 5: Assign BTP Roles to Users

```bash
# In SAP BTP Cockpit:
# 1. Go to: Security → Role Collections
# 2. Create: "UTSAV_Viewer"
#    → Add role: utsav-authority-check.Viewer
# 3. Create: "UTSAV_SecurityReviewer"
#    → Add role: utsav-authority-check.SecurityReviewer
# 4. Assign users:
#    → Security → Users → Assign Role Collections
```

---

## 🏢 Option B — Corporate Cloud Deployment

### B1 — Microsoft Azure (Azure Static Web Apps)

```bash
# Step 1: Install Azure CLI
# https://docs.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli

# Step 2: Login
az login

# Step 3: Create Resource Group
az group create \
  --name UTSAV-AuthCheck-RG \
  --location eastus

# Step 4: Create Static Web App
az staticwebapp create \
  --name utsav-authority-check \
  --resource-group UTSAV-AuthCheck-RG \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Free

# Step 5: Deploy HTML file
# Place UTSAV_Authority-Check.html in a folder called /public
# then deploy using Azure Static Web Apps CLI:

npm install -g @azure/static-web-apps-cli
swa deploy ./public \
  --app-name utsav-authority-check \
  --env production

# Your URL will be:
# https://utsav-authority-check.azurestaticapps.net
```

### B2 — Amazon AWS (S3 Static Website)

```bash
# Step 1: Install AWS CLI and configure
aws configure

# Step 2: Create S3 bucket
aws s3api create-bucket \
  --bucket utsav-authority-check \
  --region ap-south-1 \
  --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=ap-south-1

# Step 3: Enable static website hosting
aws s3 website s3://utsav-authority-check/ \
  --index-document UTSAV_Authority-Check.html

# Step 4: Set bucket policy for access
aws s3api put-bucket-policy \
  --bucket utsav-authority-check \
  --policy '{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [{
      "Sid": "PublicReadGetObject",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::utsav-authority-check/*"
    }]
  }'

# Step 5: Upload the chatbot
aws s3 cp UTSAV_Authority-Check.html \
  s3://utsav-authority-check/ \
  --content-type "text/html"

# Your URL will be:
# http://utsav-authority-check.s3-website.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com
```

### B3 — Corporate Internal Web Server (IIS / Apache / Nginx)

```bash
# ── NGINX ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Step 1: Copy file to web root
sudo cp UTSAV_Authority-Check.html /var/www/html/

# Step 2: Configure NGINX
sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/utsav-authority-check

# Paste this config:
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name utsav-authcheck.your-company.com;

    root /var/www/html;
    index UTSAV_Authority-Check.html;

    # Security headers — enforce read-only boundary [1]
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN";
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff";
    add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block";
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000";

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}

# Step 3: Enable and restart
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/utsav-authority-check \
           /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

---

## 🔒 Security Checklist Before Going Live

These checks align directly with the implementation guide requirements [1]:

```
Production Go-Live Checklist [1]:

ACCESS CONTROL
☐ Only authorized users can access the chatbot (XSUAA / Azure AD / LDAP)
☐ SAP Security team assigned as SecurityReviewer role
☐ Access matrix and approvers defined [1]

READ-ONLY BOUNDARY [1]
☐ No write connections to SAP systems enabled
☐ Production write operations disabled and tested as blocked [1]
☐ All connections verified as read-only [1]

DATA PROTECTION [1]
☐ Input masking for passwords, tokens, and emails active [1]
☐ Input retention rules approved [1]
☐ HTTPS enforced on all routes

AUDIT & MONITORING [1]
☐ Request ID logging enabled [1]
☐ Monitoring and alerting enabled [1]
☐ Support and incident contacts published [1]
☐ Full audit trail operational [1]

APPROVAL WORKFLOW [1]
☐ Human approval mandatory for all findings [1]
☐ SAP Security approval process connected [1]
☐ Change management process linked [1]
```

---

## 📊 Deployment Option Comparison

| Factor | SAP BTP | Azure | AWS S3 | Corporate Server |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SAP Integration** | ✅ Native | ⚠️ Via API | ⚠️ Via API | ✅ Direct |
| **Authentication** | ✅ XSUAA | ✅ Azure AD | ⚠️ Manual | ✅ LDAP/AD |
| **Cost** | BTP Credits | Low | Very Low | Internal IT |
| **Setup Complexity** | Medium | Low | Low | Low |
| **Best For** | SAP-native teams | Microsoft shops | AWS teams | On-premise |

---

## ✅ Recommended Deployment Path

Based on the implementation guide [1], for a SAP-native environment the recommended path is:

> **SAP BTP → Cloud Foundry → XSUAA Authentication → SAP Build Work Zone (Portal)**

This aligns with the MCP Gateway in SAP Integration Suite architecture described in the solution design [1], and ensures that authentication, audit trail, and read-only boundaries are enforced natively within the SAP ecosystem.

---

## Step 2: Prepare secure inputs
In simple words: Create one standard package so that the assistant receives complete and comparable information every time.

## What the solution is not
 It is not a replacement for SAP Security, SAP Development or Change Management.

# Deploying UTSAV_Authority-Check to SAP BTP or Corporate Cloud

Based on the implementation guide, the chatbot must be deployed following the governed architecture with read-only boundaries, full audit trail, and human approval workflows maintained throughout [1]. Here is a complete deployment guide for both options.

---

## 🏗️ Option A — SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) Deployment

### Step 1: Prerequisites & Account Setup

```
SAP BTP Requirements:
☐ SAP BTP Global Account with subaccount
☐ Cloud Foundry environment enabled
☐ SAP Build Work Zone (optional — for portal embedding)
☐ SAP Authorization & Trust Management Service (XSUAA)
☐ BTP Connectivity Service (for SAP backend connections)
☐ Destination Service configured
```

### Step 2: Prepare the Application Structure

Create the following folder structure on your local machine:

```
UTSAV_Authority-Check/
│
├── manifest.yml              ← Cloud Foundry deployment config
├── package.json              ← Node.js app descriptor
├── server.js                 ← Express web server
├── xs-security.json          ← XSUAA security config
├── xs-app.json               ← App Router config
│
└── app/
    └── UTSAV_Authority-Check.html   ← Your chatbot HTML file
```

### Step 3: Create the Server Files

**`server.js`** — Simple Express server to serve your HTML:

```javascript
// server.js
// UTSAV_Authority-Check — SAP BTP Express Server
// Read-only diagnostic tool — Implementation Guide [1]

const express = require('express');
const path    = require('path');
const app     = express();
const PORT    = process.env.PORT || 8080;

// Serve static files from /app folder
app.use(express.static(path.join(__dirname, 'app')));

// Security headers — enforce read-only boundary [1]
app.use((req, res, next) => {
    res.setHeader('X-Content-Type-Options',    'nosniff');
    res.setHeader('X-Frame-Options',           'SAMEORIGIN');
    res.setHeader('X-XSS-Protection',          '1; mode=block');
    res.setHeader('Strict-Transport-Security', 'max-age=31536000');
    res.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy',
        "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'");
    next();
});

// Root route — serve the chatbot
app.get('/', (req, res) => {
    res.sendFile(path.join(__dirname, 'app', 'UTSAV_Authority-Check.html'));
});

// Health check endpoint
app.get('/health', (req, res) => {
    res.json({
        status:    'healthy',
        app:       'UTSAV_Authority-Check',
        version:   '1.0.0',
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        boundary:  'read-only-diagnostic'
    });
});

app.listen(PORT, () => {
    console.log(`UTSAV_Authority-Check running on port ${PORT}`);
});
```

**`package.json`** — Node.js descriptor:

```json
{
  "name": "utsav-authority-check",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "SAP Authorization Check Assistant — IBM Bob + ICA",
  "main": "server.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node server.js"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.2"
  },
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=18.0.0"
  }
}
```

**`manifest.yml`** — Cloud Foundry deployment config:

```yaml
---
applications:
  - name: utsav-authority-check
    memory: 256M
    disk_quota: 512M
    instances: 1
    buildpacks:
      - nodejs_buildpack
    command: node server.js
    routes:
      - route: utsav-authority-check.<your-btp-subdomain>.cfapps.<region>.hana.ondemand.com
    env:
      NODE_ENV: production
      APP_NAME: UTSAV_Authority-Check
      BOUNDARY: read-only-diagnostic
    services:
      - utsav-xsuaa
```

**`xs-security.json`** — XSUAA security descriptor:

```json
{
  "xsappname": "utsav-authority-check",
  "tenant-mode": "dedicated",
  "description": "UTSAV Authority Check — SAP Authorization Assistant",
  "scopes": [
    {
      "name": "$XSAPPNAME.Viewer",
      "description": "View and use the authorization check assistant"
    },
    {
      "name": "$XSAPPNAME.SecurityReviewer",
      "description": "SAP Security team — approve findings"
    }
  ],
  "role-templates": [
    {
      "name": "Viewer",
      "description": "Can use the UTSAV Authority Check assistant",
      "scope-references": ["$XSAPPNAME.Viewer"]
    },
    {
      "name": "SecurityReviewer",
      "description": "SAP Security team member — can approve findings",
      "scope-references": [
        "$XSAPPNAME.Viewer",
        "$XSAPPNAME.SecurityReviewer"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**`xs-app.json`** — App Router configuration:

```json
{
  "welcomeFile": "/UTSAV_Authority-Check.html",
  "authenticationMethod": "route",
  "routes": [
    {
      "source": "^/(.*)$",
      "target": "$1",
      "localDir": "app",
      "authenticationType": "xsuaa"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Step 4: Deploy to SAP BTP — Command by Command

Open your terminal and run these commands in order:

```bash
# Step 4.1 — Login to SAP BTP Cloud Foundry
cf login -a https://api.cf.<your-region>.hana.ondemand.com \
         -u <your-email> \
         -p <your-password> \
         -o <your-org> \
         -s <your-space>

# Step 4.2 — Create XSUAA service instance
cf create-service xsuaa application utsav-xsuaa \
  -c xs-security.json

# Step 4.3 — Install Node dependencies
npm install

# Step 4.4 — Deploy the application
cf push utsav-authority-check -f manifest.yml

# Step 4.5 — Verify deployment
cf apps
cf logs utsav-authority-check --recent

# Step 4.6 — Get your public URL
cf app utsav-authority-check
```

### Step 5: Assign BTP Roles to Users

```bash
# In SAP BTP Cockpit:
# 1. Go to: Security → Role Collections
# 2. Create: "UTSAV_Viewer"
#    → Add role: utsav-authority-check.Viewer
# 3. Create: "UTSAV_SecurityReviewer"
#    → Add role: utsav-authority-check.SecurityReviewer
# 4. Assign users:
#    → Security → Users → Assign Role Collections
```

---

## 🏢 Option B — Corporate Cloud Deployment

### B1 — Microsoft Azure (Azure Static Web Apps)

```bash
# Step 1: Install Azure CLI
# https://docs.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli

# Step 2: Login
az login

# Step 3: Create Resource Group
az group create \
  --name UTSAV-AuthCheck-RG \
  --location eastus

# Step 4: Create Static Web App
az staticwebapp create \
  --name utsav-authority-check \
  --resource-group UTSAV-AuthCheck-RG \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Free

# Step 5: Deploy HTML file
# Place UTSAV_Authority-Check.html in a folder called /public
# then deploy using Azure Static Web Apps CLI:

npm install -g @azure/static-web-apps-cli
swa deploy ./public \
  --app-name utsav-authority-check \
  --env production

# Your URL will be:
# https://utsav-authority-check.azurestaticapps.net
```

### B2 — Amazon AWS (S3 Static Website)

```bash
# Step 1: Install AWS CLI and configure
aws configure

# Step 2: Create S3 bucket
aws s3api create-bucket \
  --bucket utsav-authority-check \
  --region ap-south-1 \
  --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=ap-south-1

# Step 3: Enable static website hosting
aws s3 website s3://utsav-authority-check/ \
  --index-document UTSAV_Authority-Check.html

# Step 4: Set bucket policy for access
aws s3api put-bucket-policy \
  --bucket utsav-authority-check \
  --policy '{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [{
      "Sid": "PublicReadGetObject",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::utsav-authority-check/*"
    }]
  }'

# Step 5: Upload the chatbot
aws s3 cp UTSAV_Authority-Check.html \
  s3://utsav-authority-check/ \
  --content-type "text/html"

# Your URL will be:
# http://utsav-authority-check.s3-website.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com
```

### B3 — Corporate Internal Web Server (IIS / Apache / Nginx)

```bash
# ── NGINX ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Step 1: Copy file to web root
sudo cp UTSAV_Authority-Check.html /var/www/html/

# Step 2: Configure NGINX
sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/utsav-authority-check

# Paste this config:
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name utsav-authcheck.your-company.com;

    root /var/www/html;
    index UTSAV_Authority-Check.html;

    # Security headers — enforce read-only boundary [1]
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN";
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff";
    add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block";
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000";

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}

# Step 3: Enable and restart
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/utsav-authority-check \
           /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

---

## 🔒 Security Checklist Before Going Live

These checks align directly with the implementation guide requirements [1]:

```
Production Go-Live Checklist [1]:

ACCESS CONTROL
☐ Only authorized users can access the chatbot (XSUAA / Azure AD / LDAP)
☐ SAP Security team assigned as SecurityReviewer role
☐ Access matrix and approvers defined [1]

READ-ONLY BOUNDARY [1]
☐ No write connections to SAP systems enabled
☐ Production write operations disabled and tested as blocked [1]
☐ All connections verified as read-only [1]

DATA PROTECTION [1]
☐ Input masking for passwords, tokens, and emails active [1]
☐ Input retention rules approved [1]
☐ HTTPS enforced on all routes

AUDIT & MONITORING [1]
☐ Request ID logging enabled [1]
☐ Monitoring and alerting enabled [1]
☐ Support and incident contacts published [1]
☐ Full audit trail operational [1]

APPROVAL WORKFLOW [1]
☐ Human approval mandatory for all findings [1]
☐ SAP Security approval process connected [1]
☐ Change management process linked [1]
```

---

## 📊 Deployment Option Comparison

| Factor | SAP BTP | Azure | AWS S3 | Corporate Server |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SAP Integration** | ✅ Native | ⚠️ Via API | ⚠️ Via API | ✅ Direct |
| **Authentication** | ✅ XSUAA | ✅ Azure AD | ⚠️ Manual | ✅ LDAP/AD |
| **Cost** | BTP Credits | Low | Very Low | Internal IT |
| **Setup Complexity** | Medium | Low | Low | Low |
| **Best For** | SAP-native teams | Microsoft shops | AWS teams | On-premise |

---

## ✅ Recommended Deployment Path

Based on the implementation guide [1], for a SAP-native environment the recommended path is:

> **SAP BTP → Cloud Foundry → XSUAA Authentication → SAP Build Work Zone (Portal)**

This aligns with the MCP Gateway in SAP Integration Suite architecture described in the solution design [1], and ensures that authentication, audit trail, and read-only boundaries are enforced natively within the SAP ecosystem.

Here is a complete guide for both options. --- ## 🏗️ Option A — Microsoft Teams Integration ### Step 1: Prerequisites ``` Requirements: ☐ Microsoft Teams Admin access ☐ Microsoft Azure subscription ☐ Azure Bot Service or Teams App Studio access ☐ UTSAV_Authority-Check.html (your chatbot file) ☐ Node.js 18+ installed locally ☐ Microsoft 365 Developer account (optional for testing) ``` --- ### Step 2: Prepare the Application Package Create the following folder structure: ``` UTSAV_Teams_Package/ │ ├── manifest.json ← Teams app manifest ├── color.png ← App icon (192x192 px) ├── outline.png ← App outline icon (32x32 px) │ └── app/ └── UTSAV_Authority-Check.html ``` --- ### Step 3: Create the Teams App Manifest Save this as **`manifest.json`** in your package folder: ```json { "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/teams/v1.16/MicrosoftTeams.schema.json", "manifestVersion": "1.16", "version": "1.0.0", "id": "utsav-authority-check-2026", "packageName": "com.utsav.authoritycheck", "developer": { "name": "Your Organization", "websiteUrl": "https://your-org.com", "privacyUrl": "https://your-org.com/privacy", "termsOfUseUrl": "https://your-org.com/terms" }, "name": { "short": "UTSAV_Auth-Check", "full": "UTSAV_Authority-Check — SAP Authorization Assistant" }, "description": { "short": "SAP Authorization diagnostic assistant", "full": "Governed SAP Authorization Check Assistant powered by IBM Bob, ICA and MCP Gateway. Read-only diagnostic tool — all findings require SAP Security approval." }, "icons": { "color": "color.png", "outline": "outline.png" }, "accentColor": "#1a237e", "staticTabs": [ { "entityId": "utsav-auth-check-tab", "name": "UTSAV Auth Check", "contentUrl": "https:///UTSAV_Authority-Check.html", "websiteUrl": "https:///UTSAV_Authority-Check.html", "scopes": ["personal", "team"] } ], "permissions": ["identity", "messageTeamMembers"], "validDomains": [""], "webApplicationInfo": { "id": "", "resource": "https://" } } ``` --- ### Step 4: Host the Chatbot on Azure The chatbot HTML must be hosted on a public or corporate HTTPS URL before Teams can embed it [1]: ```bash # Step 4.1 — Install Azure Static Web Apps CLI npm install -g @azure/static-web-apps-cli # Step 4.2 — Create a folder for deployment mkdir utsav-deploy cd utsav-deploy mkdir public cp /path/to/UTSAV_Authority-Check.html public/index.html # Step 4.3 — Login to Azure az login # Step 4.4 — Create Azure Static Web App az staticwebapp create \ --name utsav-authority-check \ --resource-group UTSAV-RG \ --location "East US" \ --sku Free # Step 4.5 — Deploy swa deploy ./public \ --app-name utsav-authority-check \ --env production # Your hosted URL will be: # https://utsav-authority-check.azurestaticapps.net ``` --- ### Step 5: Package and Upload to Teams ```bash # Step 5.1 — Create the Teams package ZIP # Make sure your folder contains: # manifest.json + color.png + outline.png cd UTSAV_Teams_Package zip -r UTSAV_Authority-Check_Teams.zip manifest.json color.png outline.png # Step 5.2 — Upload to Microsoft Teams # Option A — Admin Center (Org-wide deployment): # 1. Go to: https://admin.teams.microsoft.com # 2. Navigate to: Teams Apps → Manage Apps # 3. Click: Upload new app # 4. Upload: UTSAV_Authority-Check_Teams.zip # 5. Set availability: Specific users/groups or Org-wide # Option B — Teams Client (Personal/Team deployment): # 1. Open Microsoft Teams # 2. Go to: Apps → Manage your apps # 3. Click: Upload a custom app # 4. Upload: UTSAV_Authority-Check_Teams.zip ``` --- ### Step 6: Add to a Teams Channel Once uploaded, add the app to your SAP Security team channel: ``` 1. Open your SAP Security Team in Microsoft Teams 2. Click the "+" (Add a tab) button in any channel 3. Search for: "UTSAV Auth Check" 4. Select the app 5. Click: Add 6. The chatbot will now appear as a tab in your channel ``` --- ### Step 7: Configure Teams Authentication (Azure AD) To enforce that only authorized team members can use the chatbot [1]: ```javascript // Add this to UTSAV_Authority-Check.html section // for Microsoft Teams SSO authentication: ``` --- ## 🏢 Option B — SharePoint Integration ### Step 1: Host the Chatbot File The chatbot must be accessible via HTTPS before SharePoint can embed it [1]: ``` Option 1: SharePoint Document Library → Upload UTSAV_Authority-Check.html to a SharePoint document library → Share the direct link Option 2: Azure Static Web App (recommended) → Use the same hosted URL from Teams Step 4 above Option 3: SharePoint App Catalog → Package as a SharePoint Framework (SPFx) web part ``` --- ### Step 2: Embed via SharePoint Page (Simplest Method) This is the fastest way to make the chatbot available on SharePoint [1]: ``` 1. Go to your SharePoint site 2. Navigate to the page where you want the chatbot 3. Click: Edit Page 4. Click: "+" to add a new web part 5. Search for: "Embed" 6. Select: Embed web part 7. Paste your hosted chatbot URL: https://utsav-authority-check.azurestaticapps.net 8. Resize the web part to fill the page 9. Click: Publish ``` --- ### Step 3: SharePoint Framework (SPFx) Web Part (Advanced) For a fully integrated SharePoint experience, build an SPFx web part: ```bash # Step 3.1 — Install SPFx toolchain npm install -g @microsoft/generator-sharepoint npm install -g yo gulp # Step 3.2 — Generate SPFx project yo @microsoft/sharepoint # When prompted: # Solution name: utsav-authority-check # Target: SharePoint Online only # Web part name: UTSAV_Authority-Check # Framework: No JavaScript framework # Step 3.3 — Navigate to project cd utsav-authority-check ``` Edit the generated web part file: ```typescript // src/webparts/utsavAuthorityCheck/UtsavAuthorityCheckWebPart.ts import { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base'; export default class UtsavAuthorityCheckWebPart extends BaseClientSideWebPart<{}> { public render(): void { this.domElement.innerHTML = `
`; } protected get dataVersion() { return Version.parse('1.0'); } } ``` ```bash # Step 3.4 — Build and package gulp build gulp bundle --ship gulp package-solution --ship # Step 3.5 — Deploy to SharePoint App Catalog # 1. Go to SharePoint Admin Center # 2. Navigate to: More features → Apps → App Catalog # 3. Upload: sharepoint/solution/utsav-authority-check.sppkg # 4. Deploy to all sites ``` --- ### Step 4: Add to SharePoint Site ``` 1. Go to your SharePoint site 2. Click: New → Page 3. Add a web part → Search "UTSAV" 4. Select: UTSAV_Authority-Check 5. The chatbot loads inside SharePoint 6. Click: Publish ``` --- ## 🔒 Security Configuration for Both Platforms These guardrails must be maintained in all platform deployments [1]: ```javascript // Add to UTSAV_Authority-Check.html // Platform-aware security configuration const PLATFORM_CONFIG = { // Read-only boundary — enforced at all times [1] readOnly: true, // Sensitive data masking [1] maskPatterns: [ /password\s*[:=]\s*\S+/gi, /token\s*[:=]\s*\S+/gi, /bearer\s+\S+/gi, /secret\s*[:=]\s*\S+/gi ], // Human approval mandatory [1] requireApproval: true, // Full audit trail [1] auditLog: { enabled: true, fields: ['requestID', 'user', 'tool', 'timestamp', 'result'], endpoint: '/api/audit' // connect to your logging system }, // No automatic production change [1] allowProductionChange: false, // Least privilege [1] allowedAnalyzers: ['ABAP', 'SU24', 'ODATA'] }; ``` --- ## 📊 Platform Comparison | Factor | Microsoft Teams | SharePoint Embed | SharePoint SPFx | |---|---|---|---| | **Setup Complexity** | Medium | Very Low | High | | **Authentication** | ✅ Azure AD SSO | ✅ SharePoint Auth | ✅ Azure AD SSO | | **Team Collaboration** | ✅ Native channel tab | ⚠️ Page-based | ✅ Site-wide | | **Audit Trail** [1] | ✅ Teams logs + custom | ⚠️ Custom only | ✅ Full SPFx logging | | **Mobile Access** | ✅ Teams mobile app | ✅ SharePoint mobile | ✅ SharePoint mobile | | **SAP BTP Integration** | ✅ Via API | ✅ Via API | ✅ Via API | | **Best For** | Daily team usage | Quick deployment | Enterprise portal | --- ## ✅ Recommended Integration Path Based on the implementation guide [1], the recommended path for your SAP Security team is: > **Microsoft Teams tab** for daily usage → **SharePoint page** for documentation and broader access → **SAP BTP** for production MCP Gateway integration This ensures: - ✅ ICA conversational intake is accessible to all team members [1] - ✅ MCP Gateway authentication is enforced via Azure AD [1] - ✅ Full audit trail is maintained across all platforms [1] - ✅ Human approval workflow remains intact [1] - ✅ Read-only boundary is never broken [1] --- Would you like me to: 1. **Build the complete Teams bot** with proactive notifications for new findings? 2. **Create a SharePoint approval workflow** using Power Automate for finding approvals? 3. **Connect to SAP Integration Suite** as the MCP Gateway backend for production use? 4. **Add Azure AD role-based access** so only SAP Security team members can approve findings?
